yogurt — engineering design

Compiled from brief.md. Twelve entities on the mecha cluster, two screens so far, no pipeline, no hatch.

Overview

yogurt is a public network: everything a person is — their profile, their friends, their scraps, their approved testimonials, their fans, their communities and the forums inside them — is readable by everyone signed in, as it was in 2004, and everything a person does about somebody else belongs to them and is refused to everybody else. The terminal owns the door (decision 1): a passkey or a guest click, a minted handle, every screen gated. Past it, nineteen entities: the public ones, server or live as each panel's liveness asks, get their owner-write arms as additive raw policies (decision 2). What is pending — a friend request nobody has answered, a testimonial its subject has not approved — is never a public row: Electric reads the WAL and applies no policy, so a row only two people may see has to be two private rows, one in each party's scope, kept equal by triggers (decision 6): FriendRequestSent mirrored into FriendRequest, TestimonialDraft mirrored into TestimonialPending, and the public Testimonial holding approved rows alone. Karma is private too: who rated whom is the rater's business, and the smileys everyone sees are KarmaSmiley, a derived row the cluster keeps. Me is the one table the brief never names (decision 3): one live row per person, RLS-scoped to auth_uid(), provisioned by a trigger inside the auth service's insert, read as an empty-or-not probe whose :empty state is the ownership primitive (decision 4). A friendship is two rows, one per direction, minted by a trigger when a request is accepted (decision 5), so a friends list is one filter and never an OR. A forum is its members': a trigger refuses a topic or a reply from outside the community (decision 7). A fresh database already holds a living network of fifteen fictional people (decision 8), because a social network with nobody in it is not a product. The first turn built the model and two read-only screens, home and profile (decision 13); the controls — befriend, scrap, testify, fan, rate, join, post — each arrived as a form over an entity declared then, on the screen that owns it, and the rows the cluster alone writes, the smileys and the feed, arrived as derived tables kept by triggers. What a walk cannot decide is decided by three instruments: a driver over the cluster at integrate, screen tests over posed rows, and the browser journeys every release is verified with (decision 31). The identity is Scrapbook (decision 10): the pale-blue page, white panels with blue title bands, blue links and one pink. Escape hatches: none (decision 12).

Auth

auth service · mecha cluster

The door is platform doctrine and the brief designs none; the app dresses it (decision 15): the terminal's gate markup — the letter mark, the app's name, a hint, and the form — becomes a split page in shell/shared/chrome.css, the way roda's is: a header-blue panel carrying the question (quem você conhece?) and a line on what yogurt is and who is already inside, beside the form on the pale ground, where a small-capitals entrar, a passkey pill in the accent and the guest as a text link wait. The panel's words are the page's own, by language, since no catalogue reaches the gate. The mecha auth service sits behind the cluster's Caddy at /auth/*, the terminal draws the door and offers a passkey or a guest click, the server mints a handle (velvet-crow-4) and regenerates it on collision. Tokens are JWT HS256 with {role, sub, handle, exp}; PostgREST derives auth_uid() from sub, and every policy and every default auth_uid() below reads it — no screen carries the reader's id, because nothing in the binding grammar could hold one. The service's insert is (id, handle), which is why every other AppUser column is nullable or defaulted, and the 013 trigger rides that transaction to provision Me. The strip names the reader by app_user.display_name, read live, and leads to their own profile (capabilities.auth.self). Sign out clears the token and replaces the document. The door wears the Scrapbook identity: the header blue over the pale page, the wordmark in pink, the passkey outlined, the guest action quiet.

the platform’s columns

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

A person. The auth service inserts (id, handle); everything else the person fills in later from their own page. Access public: everyone reads a profile; the owner alone updates it, through 011's UPDATE arm and a column grant that keeps handle out of reach (decision 2). Relationship is stored as a message key so the reader's locale chooses the word (decision 9).

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

The asker's half of a request: private on from_id, so the sync path carries it to the asker alone and the emitted quartet lets them write and withdraw it. 015 mirrors every insert into the addressee's FriendRequest and every delete into its removal (decision 6). 011 keeps created_at the server's.

Row invariant: this.from_id != this.to_id — nobody asks themselves. UNIQUE (from_id, to_id): one request per pair.

the platform’s columns

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

The addressee's half: private on to_id, written only by the 015 mirror (011 revokes the browser INSERT, so nobody can forge a request from somebody else to themselves and accept it). The addressee's one write is accepted (011's column grant), which fires 015 to mint both friendship edges and remove both halves in the same transaction (decision 5); a delete declines and removes the asker's half too.

the platform’s columns

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

Two rows per friendship, one per direction, so a friends list is one filter on user_id and the friend is one embed (decision 5). Public, as a friends list was. No browser INSERT arm at all — every edge is the 015 trigger's — and a DELETE arm on one's own row, whose trigger takes the mirror with it.

Trustworthy, cool and sexy, zero to three each, one row per rater per rated person. Access private on rater_id: who rated whom is nobody's business but the rater's, and the emitted owner quartet is exactly right. The smileys everyone sees are an aggregate the rater's row cannot supply; KarmaSmiley holds them, kept by 023's trigger (decision 27). The rater updates their own row (023 grants it).

The smileys everyone sees: one row per rated person, the rounded mean of every rater's trustworthy, cool and sexy and how many rated, kept by 023's definer trigger on Karma and by nothing a browser holds (decision 27). Live, because its rows are born of a trigger and a server region re-reads only after its own client's write: a rating moves the smileys at once, for everyone, through the sync. id is the rated person's id. The three *_key columns are generated, the message key a screen draws for the level.

What a person did that is public, one row each, written by 024's definer triggers as a scrap is left, a testimonial published or a community joined, removed with its source. The log: since 025 nobody but the cluster reads it, and each row is fanned out into FeedItem, the inbox the screens read (decision 28). Nothing a browser holds writes here. The kind names the sentence a screen draws through kind_key, the {msg[col]} idiom.

Pipelines

None as pipeline boxes. Every number a screen shows is a count over rows the reader can see, taken in the live query, but one: the karma smileys over private Karma rows, which a definer trigger keeps in KarmaSmiley exactly on every write (decision 27); a pipeline would be a second mechanism for a mean one trigger keeps.

Screens

App entity neighbourhood · 19 entities

entities: AppUser, Community, CommunitySearch, Fan, FeedItem, FriendRequest, FriendRequestSent, Friendship, Karma, KarmaSmiley, Me, Membership, Post, Scrap, Search, Testimonial, TestimonialDraft, TestimonialPending, Topic

home screen · route /

Início: the wordmark and tagline, then two columns. On the left the reader's own panels — their card (letter disc, name, handle, city, three counts), their friends as tiles and their communities as rows — all reached through Me: the me region holds exactly the signed-in person's row and every region nested in its item reads that person's rows, so no screen ever needs the reader's id (decision 3). A fresh guest's friends and communities are empty, and each region draws its own sentence saying where to start. On the right, the network: people to meet (everyone, oldest member first, so the demo network's founders lead; a Me probe inside each tile hides the reader's own face), the newest eight scraps across every page (scrapbooks were public, so this is the pulse of the place; Scrap has two keys to AppUser and the read names each embed by its column), and every community with its category word and a member count that is a projection over the public Membership rows. Every count is a projection over rows the reader can see, read by one filter (decision 5). The strip above is the terminal's (decision 11).

Reads

  • top-level one-row list — the signed-in person (local, RLS-scoped)
  • nested one-row list in the me row — the reader's own profile columns
  • nested count — friends
  • nested count — fans
  • nested count — communities
  • nested count in the card — the copies awaiting my approval, private and live; the line links to my own testimonials page and is absent while the count's region is empty
  • nested list in the me row — the requests waiting for my answer, private and live, newest first, each row with accept and decline; no embed, so the row is the collection's and its forms resolve against it (decision 18); data-empty="Nenhum pedido esperando sua resposta."
  • nested one-row list in each request row — the asker's face, name and handle, read on their own key
  • nested list in the me row — my friends, newest nine; data-empty says where to start
  • nested list in the me row — my communities; data-empty says where to start
  • nested one-row list per membership — the category word, read from the community's own row because a row message names a column of the bound row, never of an embed
  • top-level list — people to meet
  • nested list in my card's column — my newest nine fans; data-empty="Ninguém é seu fã ainda. Deixe recados, apareça."
  • nested one-row list in my card — my own smileys, as the profile shows them; data-empty="ainda poucas avaliações"
  • top-level list — my inbox's twenty newest doings, 025's fan-out; data-empty="Nada ainda. Quando seus amigos deixarem recados, escreverem depoimentos ou entrarem em comunidades, aparece aqui."
  • nested probe per tile — "is this me" (local, RLS-scoped); its :not(:empty) hides the tile
  • top-level list — the network's newest eight scraps, writer and page owner embedded by column
  • top-level list — the twelve oldest communities, each name a link to community by id; the band's link leads to communities for the rest
  • nested count per community — members

Mutations (forms only)

  • aceitar → accepted = true on the inbox row; the 015 trigger mints both friendship rows and removes both halves (flow accept-request-home)
  • recusar → the inbox row; the mirror removes the asker's half (flow decline-request-home)
  • ser fã → one public row under a people tile, fan from the token, idol the tile's person; the unique pair refuses a second (flow be-fan-home)

Storyboard

profile screen · route /perfil/:handle

A person's page, two columns as it was: on the left the portrait panel — a large letter disc or picture, name, handle, relationship chip, friends and fans counts — and on the right the panels: quem sou eu, informações (relationship, where they live, birthday), interesses (passions, music, movies, books) and amigos as the shared person tile. The header is a one-row list over AppUser filtered on the route's handle, so every panel hydrates against that person's row; a handle nobody carries leaves the region empty and its own sentence is the whole frame. The friends list is one filter on user_id with the friend as an embed (decision 5). The controls that act on this person sit in the portrait panel: add as friend, with its four states (ask, request sent with cancel, their request with accept and decline, friends with undo), and be a fan with its two. The reader's relation to a person is read through the reader's own Me row, because Friendship and Fan rows are public and a probe on the person's id alone would answer for everybody (decision 16); the two request halves are private, so their lists are mine alone. A filter through an embed reads through PostgREST and never updates live, so every relation is read as my own rows, each nesting a one-row probe on the page's person, and the three tables are live so a row born by a trigger reaches both readers (decision 18). On the reader's own page no control is drawn and one sentence says it is theirs. A scraps panel teases the scrapbook: the newest three, the count, and one link to the page that holds them all and the box to leave one (decision 17). Testimonials and ratings are turn 15's. keep: 2: a reader bounces between two people. Reached from every tile and, for one's own page, from the reader's own name in the strip. Two panels arrived with testimonials: under the portrait, their communities newest first with the count, each a link to its page; on the right after recados, the testimonials' teaser, the newest three approved with the count in the band's link and the foot's link to the box (decision 22).

Reads

  • top-level one-row list — the person; data-empty="Ninguém com esse nome por aqui."
  • nested count — friends
  • nested count — fans
  • nested list — the teaser, author:app_user!author_id(handle,display_name,photo_url), newest first; data-empty="Nenhum recado ainda."
  • nested one-row probe in every teased scrap — I wrote it; its stamped child hides "responder"
  • nested count — all of them, beside the link to the scrapbook
  • nested list — the testimonials' teaser, the newest three approved; a live table, so the writer is the nested region below and not an embed
  • nested one-row list in each teaser row — the writer's name and handle, on their own key
  • nested count — all of them, in the band's link to testimonials
  • nested list under the portrait — their communities, newest first, each name a link to community; server-durable and form-free, so the embed is safe
  • nested count — all their communities, in the band
  • nested list — their newest twelve friends; each tile links profile by the friend's handle; the band's link, with the count, leads to friends
  • nested probe in the person row — "is this my page"; its :not(:empty) hides every control and shows the own-page sentence
  • nested one-row list in the person row — the reader's own row, the context my relation rows below read through (decision 16)
  • nested list in the me row — my friendships, live; each row nests the person probe below and carries the unfriend form (decision 18)
  • nested probe in each of my friendship rows — "is this friend the page's person"; the arms box reads :has() over it
  • nested probe in the me row — "am I their fan"
  • nested one-row list under the counts — the smileys everyone sees; data-empty="ninguém avaliou ainda"
  • nested one-row list in my friendship row — my own rating of this friend, private; data-empty="você ainda não avaliou", whose stamp draws the create form
  • nested list in the person row — my sent requests, private and live; each row nests the person probe and carries the cancel form
  • nested probe in each sent row — "is this request to the page's person"
  • nested list in the person row — my inbox, private and live; each row nests the person probe and carries accept and decline
  • nested probe in each inbox row — "is this request from the page's person"

Mutations (forms only)

  • add as friend → one private row, to_id the person's; the 015 mirror writes their inbox half (flow ask-friend)
  • cancel → the row of my sent list that names the person; the mirror removes their half (flow withdraw-request)
  • accept → accepted = true on the inbox row, row-scoped; 015 mints both edges and removes both halves (flow accept-request)
  • decline → the inbox row, row-scoped; the mirror removes their sent half (flow decline-request)
  • undo → the row of my friendship probe, my half; the unmirror takes theirs (flow unfriend)
  • be a fan → one public row, idol_id the person's (flow be-fan)
  • stop → the row of my fan probe (flow unfan)
  • avaliar → one private row, rater from the token, rated the friendship row's friend, three levels as numbers (flow rate)
  • avaliar again → the three levels on my own row for this friend (flow rate-again)
  • retirar avaliação → my own row for this friend, one tap; the trigger recounts or drops the smileys (flow unrate)

Storyboard

scrapbook screen · route /recados/:handle

A person's scrapbook, as the "recados" tab was: the person's name and how many scraps they have, the box to leave one, and every scrap on their page newest first — the writer's face and name as a link, when it was left, and what it says. The header is a one-row list over AppUser filtered on the route's handle, exactly as profile reads it, so a handle nobody carries is the same sentence on both. The list is one filter on owner_id with the writer as an embed named by its column, because Scrap has two keys to AppUser. Leaving a scrap is a create whose writer is the token's bearer; the row's hidden owner_id is the page. Deleting is row-scoped inside each scrap's row, and the control is drawn only for the reader who may: two one-row probes on the reader's own Me row, one filtered on the writer's id and one on the owner's, and the row draws "apagar…" when either has a row; it takes two taps, as unfriend does, the summary arming a red "sim, apagar" (decision 17). Under every scrap, "responder" leads to the writer's own scrapbook, which is where a reply was left in 2004. The box sits above the list, because leaving one is why the page was opened; on success it clears, focus rests on the button, and the new row is the list's first; line breaks typed are kept. The profile's scraps panel carries two links here, the band's to read on and the foot's to the box. Reached from the profile's scraps panel and from "responder" anywhere a scrap is shown; back goes to the person's profile.

Reads

  • top-level one-row list — the person; data-empty="Ninguém com esse nome por aqui."
  • nested count — how many scraps the person has
  • nested list — every scrap on the page, newest first; data-empty="Ninguém deixou recado aqui ainda. Seja a primeira pessoa."
  • nested one-row probe in every scrap row — I wrote it
  • nested one-row probe in every scrap row — it is on my page

Mutations (forms only)

  • leave → one public row, writer from the token, owner from the page (flow leave-scrap)
  • sim, apagar → the enclosing scrap's row, after "apagar…" armed it; 011 lets its writer or the page's owner; a refusal paints its sentence beside the button (flow delete-scrap)

credits screen · route /creditos

The pictures' authors and licenses, as assets/manifest.json records them: the portraits are randomuser.me's, free to use; the ten community pictures are Wikimedia Commons files under CC BY and CC BY-SA terms, each named with its author and its page, which is what attribution asks (decision 30). Static markup, no region: the manifest is the source, this page is written from it, and the pictures test holds the two together. Reached from the directory's foot; not in the strip.

        Storyboard

        communities screen · route /comunidades

        Every community, by category, as the "comunidades" directory was: a line that says so, the search box, then one banded section per category in one fixed order — humor, música, cinema e TV, comida e bebida, computadores e internet, esportes, viagens, cidades e bairros, escolas e faculdades, outros — each community a row with its picture, its name and its member count. Each section is a public read of Community filtered on its category word; a category with no community draws no section. The search is a row: one tab CommunitySearch row the form upserts, and a results section nested in it reads name=ilike.*{q}*; a blank q draws no results panel. Creating is a form right under the search, so "no community by that name" is one glance from the box that makes one: name, category as a select over the ten words, description; the owner is the token's bearer, a guest's as much as anyone's, and the new row lands in its section on the next read; a directory with no community at all says so above the sections (decision 19). Reached from the strip and from início's communities band; a community's page is the next turn's, so names are not links yet.

        • top-level one-row probe above the sections — "does any community exist"; its data-empty is the sentence that sells the first one
        • top-level list, one per category word in the fixed order — the section; data-empty="" and the section hides when empty
        • nested count in every row — members

        Mutations (forms only)

        • buscar → the search row's q (flow search-communities)
        • criar comunidade → one public row, owner from the token (flow create-community)

        Storyboard

        community screen · route /comunidade/:id

        A community's page, two columns as the profile is: on the left the community panel — picture or letter, name, category chip, member count, the owner's name as a link read on their own key, and the arm; on the right quem somos, membros as the shared person tile capped at twelve with the full count in the band, and fórum. The header is a one-row list over Community filtered on the route's id; an id nobody carries leaves it empty and its own sentence is the frame. The arm is read the way the profile reads a relation: a one-row Me region nests a Membership probe filtered on my id and the route's id, with no embed, and :has() over it draws either "entrar na comunidade" (a create, the community's id hidden) or "você é membro" with a one-tap "sair da comunidade" whose delete is row-scoped inside the probe's row, one tap since rejoining is free (decision 23). The owner sees "editar comunidade", description and photo link filled from the row, drawn by a Me probe on owner_id; the update is row-scoped in the community's own row and 011 admits the owner alone. The member count and the band's link lead to members. The forum is Topic filtered on the community, newest first, each row the title, the opener through the author embed, when, and the replies counted over Post, the title a link to topic carrying the community's id and the topic's; the new-topic form heads it and is drawn for members alone, the same :has(), while the 017 guard remains the truth a hand-made request meets (decision 20). keep: 2. Reached from every community name on início and the directory; back goes to the directory.

        • nested one-row list in the community row — the reader's own row, the context the probe reads through
        • nested probe in the me row — "am I a member"; its row carries the leave form
        • nested list — the newest twelve members as person tiles; data-empty="Ninguém entrou ainda."
        • nested list — the forum's topics, newest first, each title a link to topic; data-empty="Nenhum tópico ainda. Quem é membro pode abrir o primeiro."
        • nested count in every topic row — replies
        • nested probe in the community row — "am I the owner"; its stamped child draws the edit form

        Storyboard

        topic screen · route /comunidade/:community/topico/:id

        One thread, as the forum's thread page was: the title, who opened it and when, the community it belongs to as a link, the opening message, and every reply oldest first — a thread reads top-down — each with the writer's face, name and time. The header is a one-row list over Topic filtered on the route's id; the route carries the community's id too, so the membership probe can read through the reader's Me row on {param.community} alone, the way the community page reads it, and draw the reply box for members with the note for everyone else while the 017 guard remains the rule. Replies are Post filtered on the topic, oldest first, the reply box last; a reply the reader wrote carries "apagar…" through a Me probe on its author_id, arming a red "sim, apagar" whose delete is row-scoped (decision 21). The runtime stamps loading, populated, empty and validation-error on the screen; member and deleting are frame names, the probe's stamped child and the open details telling them apart on the live page, as the community page's member and owner are. keep: 2. Reached from every title on a community's forum; back goes to the community the route names, on the unknown address too, since the route carries it whether or not the topic exists.

        Reads

        • top-level one-row list — the topic with its opener and its community; data-empty="Nenhum tópico com esse endereço: apagado, ou nunca existiu."
        • nested one-row list in the topic row — the reader's own row, the context the probe reads through
        • nested probe in the me row — "am I a member of this topic's community"; its stamped child draws the reply box
        • nested list — the replies, oldest first; data-empty="Ninguém respondeu ainda."
        • nested one-row probe in every reply — I wrote it; its stamped child draws "apagar…"
        • nested one-row probe in the topic row — I opened it; its stamped child draws "apagar tópico…" while the reply count stamps nothing
        • nested count in the replies band

        Mutations (forms only)

        • responder → one public row, writer from the token, topic from the page; the 017 guard refuses a non-member (flow reply)
        • sim, apagar → the enclosing reply's row, after "apagar…" armed it; 011 lets its writer alone (flow delete-reply)
        • sim, apagar o tópico → the topic's own row, after "apagar tópico…" armed it; 022 lets its opener alone and refuses while a reply exists (flow delete-topic)

        Storyboard

        testimonials screen · route /depoimentos/:handle

        A person's testimonials, as the "depoimentos" tab was: their name and how many, and every approved one newest first with the writer's face, name and time. The header is the same one-row list over AppUser as profile, so a handle nobody carries is the same sentence. The box draws for a friend who has none about this person yet: my friendship rows, read through my own Me row, each probed on the page's person, the way the profile reads its arm. Writing is a create on TestimonialDraft, private to me, which the 015 mirror copies into the subject's TestimonialPending; the 021 guard refuses a non-friend and a second one about the same person. My waiting draft shows under "esperando aprovação" with a two-tap "retirar…". On my own page the Me probe hides the box and the pending copies head the page, each with "aprovar", an update of the one word the subject may write, which the 015 publish trigger turns into the public Testimonial row, and a two-tap "recusar…". An approved one carries "apagar…" for its writer or its subject, two Me probes as the scrapbook's. All three tables are live, so a draft reaches the subject's open page and the approval reaches both parties' without a reload; none of the lists carries an embed, the writer being a nested region on their own key (decision 22). keep: 2. Reached from the profile's depoimentos panel and from início's line; back goes to the profile.

        Reads

        • top-level one-row list — the person; data-empty="Ninguém com esse nome por aqui."
        • nested count — how many approved
        • nested probe in the person row — "is this my page"; its stamped child hides the box and shows the pending panel
        • nested one-row list in the person row — the reader's own row, the context the friendship rows read through
        • nested list in the me row — my friendships, live; each row nests the person probe
        • nested probe in each of my friendship rows — "is this friend the page's person"; the box reads its stamped child
        • nested list — the copies awaiting my approval, private and live, newest first; drawn on my own page alone, with rows alone
        • nested list — my own waiting drafts about this person, private and live; drawn with rows alone
        • nested list — every approved one, newest first; data-empty="Ninguém deixou um depoimento ainda."
        • nested one-row list in every pending and approved row — the writer's name and handle, on their own key
        • nested probe in every approved row — I wrote it; any such row also hides the box, since one per person is the rule
        • nested probe in every approved row — it is about me

        Mutations (forms only)

        • enviar depoimento → one private row, writer from the token, subject from the page; 015 mirrors it; 021 refuses a non-friend or a second one (flow write-testimonial)
        • sim, retirar → the enclosing draft's row, after "retirar…" armed it; 015 removes the subject's copy (flow withdraw-testimonial)
        • aprovar → approved on the enclosing pending row; 015 publishes the public row and removes both halves (flow approve-testimonial)
        • sim, recusar → the enclosing pending row, after "recusar…" armed it; 015 removes the writer's half (flow discard-testimonial)
        • sim, apagar → the enclosing approved row, after "apagar…" armed it; 011 lets its writer or its subject (flow delete-testimonial)

        edit screen · route /editar-perfil

        The reader's own form, as "editar perfil" was: my AppUser row read through my Me row, every column I may write as a control filled from it, name, photo link, who I am, relationship, city, country, birthday and the four interests, and one "salvar". The update is row-scoped in that nested row and 011 grants exactly these columns on one's own row, so nobody edits anyone else's. A control I touched keeps my text while the row re-reads; on save the row re-reads with what I wrote, and the profile and the strip, which read the same row, show it on their next read. The page has no own-page probe: the me row is the page (decision 23). Reached from início's card and from the sentence on my own profile; back goes to my profile.

        members screen · route /membros/:id

        A community's full member list, as its "membros" page was: the community's name and how many, then every member as the shared person tile, newest first. The header is the same one-row list over Community as community, so an id nobody carries is the same sentence. The list is one filter on community_id with the person as an embed, safe here since Membership is server-durable and the page carries no form, the same read the community page caps at twelve. Reached from the community page's count and its band link; back goes to the community.

        • nested count — how many members

        Storyboard

        search screen · route /buscar

        The strip's "buscar", as the 2004 top bar had it: one box that finds people by name or username and communities by name. The box is the directory's idiom (decision 19): one Search tab row, mine alone, which the form upserts, and two lists nested in it that read its q as a case-folded contains, AppUser on search_text, a generated column that is the display name and the username in one, Community on the name; people as the shared person tile, communities as the directory's row with the member count. A blank q hides both panels through the attribute bound to it and leaves the hint; a q that matches nothing gets each panel's own sentence (decision 24). The runtime stamps loading and populated; searching and search-none are frame names, the bound attribute and each list's own sentence telling them apart live. The word survives in-app navigation, as a tab row does; a hard reload starts blank, since the tab store the terminal keeps across a reload holds the theme and the token alone, a seam recorded for the harvest. Reached from the strip on every screen.

        Reads

        • top-level one-row list — the tab row the box upserts; an empty row with a blank q is bound when none exists, so the box draws on first visit
        • nested list — people whose search_text, the generated column holding the name and the username, contains q; data-empty="Ninguém com esse nome."
        • nested list — communities whose name contains q; data-empty="Nenhuma comunidade com esse nome."
        • nested count per row — members
        • nested one-row probe in every people tile — this person is me; its stamped child hides "ser fã"

        Mutations (forms only)

        • buscar → the one tab row's q; nothing leaves the tab (flow do-search)
        • ser fã → one public row under a people tile; the unique pair refuses a second (flow be-fan-search)

  a["reader types and taps buscar"] --> b["upsert the tab row: q"] --> S[("Search")]
  S -. "the two nested lists re-read on q: people by name or handle, communities by name" .-> page["search: searching"]
  S -. "a blank q: no panel, the hint" .-> blank["search: populated"]

        Invariants & test pairs

        Prose invariants with embedded CEL, translated to executable tests at the program rung. Bindings are injected, never ambient: input is the given data plus input.now, output the result, error the failure (error.kind, error.field). Failures are spelled one way each: 'check_violation' for a row CHECK or NOT NULL, 'unique_violation' for a composite unique (its error.field is the constraint name), 'rls_denied' for a write matching no policy, 'unauthorized' for no token.

        auth

        A passkey or guest click yields a token whose bearer the network can name: output.handle.size() > 0 && output.role == 'app_user'. The auth service inserts AppUser (id, handle) and the 013 trigger provisions Me in the same transaction, so output.me.id == output.user_id holds on the first paint — which is what lets home draw the reader's own card at once rather than after a CDC round trip. A passkey holder is named in the strip beside sign out; a guest is offered a passkey there instead, since the terminal mints a guest a new identity on sign-out and offers no way out of one.

        Me

        The me read returns exactly one row under its own token and nothing under anybody else's: output.mine.size() == 1 && output.mine[0].id == input.user_id && output.as_other_filtered_on_mine == [] — the second clause is the read a second person makes, filtered on the first's id. That is what makes an empty probe region mean "not mine" on every screen, and every browser write against it is refused because 012 drops the arms that private emits.

        home

        The people rail reads everyone, oldest member first — output.rows.size() >= input.people_seeded && range(output.rows.size() - 1).all(i, output.rows[i].created_at <= output.rows[i + 1].created_at) — so the demo network's founders lead. The reader's own row is in that read; the Me probe inside their tile is what hides it, so the hidden half is a DOM claim over the rendered screen under a real token: output.visible_tiles.all(t, t.handle != output.reader.handle).

        The network's latest scraps are the newest eight across every page, newest first, each carrying its writer's and its page owner's handle: output.size() == input.cap && range(output.size() - 1).all(i, output[i].created_at >= output[i + 1].created_at) && output.all(s, s.author.handle.size() > 0 && s.owner.handle.size() > 0 && s.author.handle != s.owner.handle). Scrap has two keys to AppUser, so the read names each embed by its column; an embed that resolved the wrong key would make writer and owner the same person on every row.

        Every community is listed, oldest first, with its category word and a member count equal to its Membership rows: output.rail.size() == input.communities_seeded && output.rail[0].name == input.first && output.rail[0].members == input.first_members && range(output.rail.size() - 1).all(i, output.rail[i].created_at <= output.rail[i + 1].created_at) && output.rail.all(c, c.category_label.size() > 0 && c.members == output.counts[c.id]). output.counts is an independent read of membership grouped by community, so the projection is checked against the table and not against itself; the count is a projection over rows everyone can see, so it is exact without a sink (pipelines).

        A fresh guest's own friends and communities regions resolve to the empty collection and draw exactly the shipped sentence, each naming where to start, while the network panels beside them are full; a seeded member's same regions are full and carry no sentence: output.guest.my_friends == [] && output.guest.my_communities == [] && output.guest.my_friends_copy == output.messages[input.friends_message] && output.guest.my_communities_copy == output.messages[input.communities_message] && output.guest.network_scraps.size() > 0 && output.member.my_friends.size() == input.member_friends && output.member.my_communities.size() == input.member_communities && output.member.my_friends_copy == '' && output.frames.fresh != output.frames.populated. The member half is what makes the guest half falsifiable: a filter on the wrong key would be empty for everyone and the sentence would show to a person with six communities. The terminal's state is populated for both; fresh is the storyboard's name for the guest's frame, and the last clause holds the two frames apart.

        A face and a letter are the two states of one box. A person whose photo_url is a link binds it into the face's img and draws no disc; a person with none — the fresh guest — binds the binder's transparent pixel, a data: src that fetches nothing, and the disc with their handle's first letter shows exactly then: output.with_photo.src_is_pixel == false && output.with_photo.disc_visible == false && output.without_photo.src_is_pixel == true && output.without_photo.disc_visible == true && output.without_photo.disc_text.startsWith(output.without_photo.handle[0:1]) && output.community_with_photo.src_is_pixel == false && output.community_with_photo.disc_visible == false && output.community_without_photo.src_is_pixel == true && output.community_without_photo.disc_visible == true. The community pair ("Eu amo pizza" with a picture, "Eu falo sozinho" without) holds the same rule on the rail. The two states are decided by the bound value, never by whether an image loaded, so a missing link can never draw a broken glyph (decision 14).

        The gate is the terminal's markup dressed by the app: the intro names the app, the headline asks the question and the line says who is inside, in the page's language; both roads are offered, and one tap on the guest control yields a session and lands on início — output.intro_name == 'yogurt' && output.headline == 'quem você conhece?' && output.line.size() > 0 && output.passkey_control_present == true && output.guest_click_lands == 'home' && output.session.user.guest == true. The door precedes início in the first_load path, which is where accept-door is walked.

        A person's scrapbook is every public scrap whose owner is that person, newest first, each carrying when it was left and its writer's handle through the author embed, which is the writer's and not the owner's: in the demo network the two never coincide, so an embed on the wrong key would show the owner on every row; the count the profile shows is the same rows counted: output.rows.size() == input.owner_scraps && output.count == output.rows.size() && output.rows.all(s, s.owner_id == input.owner && s.author.handle.size() > 0 && s.author.handle != output.owner_handle && s.created_at.size() > 0) && range(output.rows.size() - 1).all(i, output.rows[i].created_at >= output.rows[i + 1].created_at).

        Leaving a scrap inserts one public row whose writer is the token's bearer and whose owner is the page, and the page's next read has it first; a blank body, a body of spaces alone or an over-long one is refused by the row CHECK, a forged writer by RLS, and nothing else about the row is the client's to say: output.row.author_id == input.author && output.row.owner_id == input.owner && output.row.body == input.body && output.after_count == output.before_count + 1 && output.after_rows[0].id == output.row.id && output.blank.kind == 'check_violation' && output.spaces.kind == 'check_violation' && output.long.kind == 'check_violation' && output.forged.kind == 'rls_denied'.

        A scrap is deleted by its writer or by the owner of the page it is on, and by nobody else: the 011 policy is the OR of the two, so a third person's delete matches no policy and removes nothing; and the control is drawn for the same two readers alone, because each row's two Me probes are empty for everyone else: output.by_author.control_visible && output.by_author.gone && output.by_owner.control_visible && output.by_owner.gone && !output.by_third.control_visible && output.by_third.kind == 'rls_denied' && !output.by_third.gone.

        The profile's scraps panel is the scrapbook's newest three, in the scrapbook's order, with a count of all of them in the band's link and the foot's link to the box; a person with none gets the panel's own sentence and the same foot link, never a blank: output.full.teaser.size() == (output.full.total < input.cap ? output.full.total : input.cap) && output.full.link_count == output.full.total && output.full.leave_link.size() > 0 && range(output.full.teaser.size() - 1).all(i, output.full.teaser[i].created_at >= output.full.teaser[i + 1].created_at) && output.none.teaser.size() == 0 && output.none.empty_text.size() > 0 && output.none.leave_link.size() > 0.

        An accept is seen by both parties without a reload: the request halves and the friendship are live, so the addressee's accept (their own write) empties their inbox and the trigger-born friendship rows reach both readers through the sync shape; each profile's arms move to friends and each friends count moves by one, on the page that was already open; a decline reaches the asker the same way, their control back to add as friend with no sentence, as the original allowed; a reverse pair that predates the guard is cleared by the accept, both halves: output.addressee.before.visible_arms == ['accept-request', 'decline-request', 'be-fan'] && output.addressee.after.visible_arms == ['unfriend', 'unfan'] && !output.addressee.after.reloaded && output.asker.after.visible_arms == ['unfriend', 'unfan'] && !output.asker.after.reloaded && output.addressee.after.friends_count == output.addressee.before.friends_count + 1 && output.asker.after.friends_count == output.asker.before.friends_count + 1 && output.declined.asker.visible_arms == ['ask-friend', 'be-fan'] && !output.declined.asker.reloaded && output.declined.asker.note == '' && output.reverse_pair.after_accept.sent == [] && output.reverse_pair.after_accept.inbox == [].

        Início lists every request addressed to the reader — the private inbox half, mine alone — newest first with the asker's name, and each row's accept or decline removes it on the spot; a reader with none gets the panel's own sentence: output.pending.size() == output.inbox_count && output.pending.all(r, r.from.handle.size() > 0 && r.to_id == input.reader) && output.after_accept.pending.size() == output.pending.size() - 1 && output.after_accept.friends_count == output.friends_count + 1 && output.after_decline.pending.size() == output.after_accept.pending.size() - 1 && output.none.empty_text.size() > 0.

        A person's friends page is every friendship row whose user is that person, each with the friend through the embed; the profile's amigos panel is the newest twelve of the same rows with the full count in its link; a handle nobody carries is the same sentence as the profile's: output.rows.size() == output.count && output.rows.all(f, f.user_id == input.person && f.friend.handle.size() > 0) && output.profile.tiles.size() == (output.count < input.cap ? output.count : input.cap) && output.profile.link_count == output.count && output.unknown.empty_text.size() > 0.

        The comunidades page is ten category sections in one fixed order, each a public read filtered on its category word, so every community appears exactly once under its own category with its member count and its picture or its letter, and a category with no community draws no section; a directory with no community says so: output.drawn_total == output.total && output.sections.all(s, s.rows.size() > 0 && s.rows.all(c, c.category == s.category && c.members == c.membership_rows)) && output.sections.size() == output.categories_with_rows && output.order == input.order && output.sections.all(s, s.rows.all(c, c.has_picture ? c.photo_visible : c.disc_visible)) && output.empty_directory.sentence.size() > 0.

        A search is one tab row, mine alone, whose q the results region reads as a case-folded contains on the name (ASCII case; accents are not folded, so the fixture carries none); a blank q draws no results panel at all, and a q that matches nothing gets the panel's own sentence: output.hits.size() == output.expected && output.hits.all(c, c.name.lowerAscii().contains(input.q.lowerAscii())) && output.none.hits.size() == 0 && output.none.empty_text.size() > 0 && output.blank.panel_hidden.

        Creating inserts one public row whose owner is the token's bearer, with a name, one of the ten category words and a description; it is drawn under its category on the next read; a blank name or a word outside the ten is refused by the row CHECK, a forged owner by RLS; a second community with the same name is accepted, as the original accepted its thousand clones: output.row.owner_id == input.owner && output.row.category == input.category && output.row.name == input.name && output.in_section && output.after_count == output.before_count + 1 && output.blank_name.kind == 'check_violation' && output.bad_category.kind == 'check_violation' && output.forged_owner.kind == 'rls_denied' && output.duplicate_name.row.name == input.name.

        A community's page is its public row by the route's id with the owner read on their own key and the members counted over the public membership rows, the newest twelve of them drawn; an id nobody carries is the region's own sentence with the way back to the directory; every community name on início and the directory is a link here carrying the row's id: output.page.name == input.name && output.page.category == output.row.category && output.page.owner_handle == output.owner.handle && output.page.member_count == output.membership_rows && output.members.size() == (output.membership_rows < input.cap ? output.membership_rows : input.cap) && output.unknown.empty_text.size() > 0 && output.unknown.back_route == 'communities' && output.links.all(l, l.route == 'community' && l.id == output.row.id).

        Joining inserts one public membership row taking its user from the token; the count moves and my membership probe, read through my me row, flips the arm to leave, on this visit and the next; leaving is one tap, since rejoining is free; joining twice is refused by the pair's unique; leaving is a row-scoped delete of my own row and the arm flips back; a forged user is refused by RLS: output.joined.row.user_id == input.user && output.joined.row.community_id == input.community && output.joined.count == output.before_count + 1 && output.joined.visible_arms == ['leave-community'] && output.revisit.visible_arms == ['leave-community'] && output.again.kind == 'unique_violation' && output.left.taps == 1 && output.left.count == output.before_count && output.left.visible_arms == ['join-community'] && output.forged.kind == 'rls_denied'.

        The forum is the community's topics newest first, each with its opener through the author embed and its replies counted over the public posts; a member's new topic lands first on the next read and the form is drawn for members alone; a non-member sees no form and the note, and the 017 guard refuses their insert as a CHECK would; a blank title and a blank body are each refused by the row CHECK: output.topics.size() == output.topic_rows && range(output.topics.size() - 1).all(i, output.topics[i].created_at >= output.topics[i + 1].created_at) && output.topics.all(t, t.author.handle.size() > 0 && t.replies == t.post_rows) && output.member.posted.title == input.title && output.member.after[0].id == output.member.posted.id && output.member.form_visible && output.outsider.kind == 'check_violation' && !output.outsider.form_visible && output.outsider.note.size() > 0 && output.blank_title.kind == 'check_violation' && output.blank_body.kind == 'check_violation'.

        A topic's page is its public row by the route's id with its opener through the author embed, and its replies are the public posts on it oldest first, each with its writer through the embed, as many as the forum counted; an id nobody carries is the region's own sentence with the way back to the community; every topic title on a community's forum is a link here carrying the community's id and the topic's: output.page.title == output.row.title && output.page.opener_handle == output.author.handle && output.page.body == output.row.body && output.replies.size() == output.post_rows && range(output.replies.size() - 1).all(i, output.replies[i].created_at <= output.replies[i + 1].created_at) && output.replies.all(r, r.author.handle.size() > 0) && output.unknown.empty_text.size() > 0 && output.unknown.back_route == 'community' && output.links.all(l, l.route == 'topic' && l.id == output.row.id && l.community == output.row.community_id).

        A reply inserts one public row whose writer is the token's bearer and whose topic is the page; it lands last on the next read and the count moves; the box is drawn for members of the topic's community alone, read through the me row on the route's community, while the 017 guard refuses a non-member's insert as a CHECK would; a blank body or spaces alone are refused by the row CHECK, each refusal drawn under the box with the text kept; the outsider's forced insert saves nothing: output.member.posted.body == input.body && output.member.after[output.member.after.size() - 1].id == output.member.posted.id && output.member.count == output.before_count + 1 && output.member.form_visible && output.outsider.kind == 'check_violation' && output.outsider.saved == 0 && !output.outsider.form_visible && output.outsider.note.size() > 0 && output.blank.kind == 'check_violation' && output.blank.sentence_visible && output.spaces.kind == 'check_violation' && output.spaces.sentence_visible && output.spaces.kept == input.spaces.

        A reply is deleted by its writer alone, in two taps, the first of which deletes nothing; the control is drawn for the writer alone by a Me probe on author_id in the reply's row, and the 011 policy refuses anyone else: output.by_author.control_visible && output.by_author.armed.count == output.by_author.count && output.by_author.gone && !output.by_other.control_visible && output.by_other.kind == 'rls_denied' && !output.by_other.gone.

        A person's depoimentos page is the public rows whose subject is the route's person, newest first, each writer read on their own key, as many as the band counts; the profile's panel teases the newest three with the count in a link to the page; a handle nobody carries is the same sentence as the profile's: output.page.rows.size() == output.count && range(output.page.rows.size() - 1).all(i, output.page.rows[i].created_at >= output.page.rows[i + 1].created_at) && output.page.rows.all(r, r.author.handle.size() > 0 && r.subject_id == output.person.id) && output.teaser.size() == min(3, output.count) && output.teaser_link.route == 'testimonials' && output.teaser_link.count == output.count && output.unknown.empty_text.size() > 0.

        A friend's write inserts one private draft whose writer is the token's bearer and whose subject is the page, and the 015 mirror gives the subject a pending copy with the same id; the public table does not move; the writer's page shows the draft under esperando aprovação with the box, drawn for friends alone through my friendship rows each probed on the page's person; the 021 guard refuses a non-friend and a second one about a person with an approved one as a CHECK would, the unique pair refuses a second draft, the invariant refuses oneself, and a blank body is refused by the row CHECK; the box is hidden for a writer whose approved one is on the page: output.friend.draft.subject_id == input.subject && output.friend.draft.author_id == input.friend && output.friend.pending_for_subject.id == output.friend.draft.id && output.friend.public_rows == output.public_before && output.friend.waiting_visible && output.friend.form_visible && output.stranger.kind == 'check_violation' && !output.stranger.form_visible && output.stranger.note.size() > 0 && output.blank.kind == 'check_violation' && output.blank.sentence_visible && output.second.kind == 'check_violation' && output.self.kind == 'check_violation' && output.done.kind == 'check_violation' && !output.done.form_visible && output.done.note.size() > 0 && output.twice.kind == 'unique_violation'.

        A pending copy reaches the subject's open page without a reload; setting approved publishes the public row with the same id and removes both halves, and the public row reaches both parties' open pages live; a discard removes both halves and publishes nothing; the first tap of either arms and changes nothing: output.arrival.subject_saw_pending_live && output.approve.public.id == output.approve.pending.id && output.approve.draft_gone && output.approve.pending_gone && output.approve.subject_sees_public_live && output.approve.writer_sees_public_live && output.discard.public_rows == output.discard.public_before && output.discard.draft_gone && output.discard.pending_gone && output.armed.count == output.before_count.

        An approved testimonial is deleted by its writer or its subject alone, in two taps; the control is drawn for those two by two Me probes in the row, and the 011 policy refuses anyone else: output.by_author.control_visible && output.by_author.gone && output.by_subject.control_visible && output.by_subject.gone && !output.by_third.control_visible && output.by_third.kind == 'rls_denied' && !output.by_third.gone.

        A profile's comunidades panel is the person's memberships newest first, at most twelve, each the community's name as a link to its page by id with its picture or letter, and the band's count is all of them: output.panel.size() == min(12, output.count) && range(output.panel.size() - 1).all(i, output.panel[i].created_at >= output.panel[i + 1].created_at) && output.panel.all(t, t.link.route == 'community' && t.link.id == t.community_id && t.name.size() > 0) && output.count_shown == output.count.

        Início's line counts the reader's own pending copies, is absent when none waits, links to the reader's own depoimentos page, and moves when a draft arrives, the table being live: output.line.count == output.pending_rows && (output.pending_rows > 0 ? output.line.visible : !output.line.visible) && output.line.route == 'testimonials' && output.line.handle == output.me.handle && output.line.moved_live.

        The edit page reads my own row through the me row and fills every control from it; saving updates that row alone, within the columns 011 grants, and the profile and the strip show the new values on their next read; another person's row is refused by RLS, a photo link that is not https or a name over sixty characters by the row CHECK, each refusal painting its sentence; a cleared birthday saves as null: output.saved.row.id == output.me.id && output.saved.row.display_name == input.display_name && output.saved.row.about == input.about && output.saved.row.relationship == input.relationship && output.saved.row.birthday == input.birthday && output.saved.profile_shows && output.saved.strip_name == input.display_name && output.prefilled.all(f, f.value == f.column_value) && output.other.kind == 'rls_denied' && output.bad_photo.kind == 'check_violation' && output.bad_photo.sentence_visible && output.long_name.kind == 'check_violation' && output.blank_birthday.row.birthday == null && output.links.card == '/editar-perfil' && output.links.own_profile == '/editar-perfil'.

        The community page draws the edit form for its owner alone, a Me probe on owner_id, filled from the row; saving updates description and photo link in place and the page shows them on its next read; a member's hand-made update is refused by RLS and a photo link that is not https by the row CHECK, each refusal painting its sentence: output.owner.form_visible && output.owner.saved.description == input.description && output.owner.saved.photo_url == input.photo_url && output.owner.page_shows && !output.member.form_visible && output.member.kind == 'rls_denied' && output.bad_photo.kind == 'check_violation' && output.bad_photo.sentence_visible.

        A community's members page is every membership of it, newest first, each the person's tile linking to their profile, as many as the band counts; the page's count and the band's link on the community page lead here; an id nobody carries is the region's own sentence with the way back: output.page.tiles.size() == output.count && output.page.tiles.all(t, t.link.route == 'profile' && t.handle.size() > 0) && range(output.page.tiles.size() - 1).all(i, output.page.tiles[i].created_at >= output.page.tiles[i + 1].created_at) && output.band_link.route == 'members' && output.band_link.id == input.community && output.count_link.route == 'members' && output.unknown.empty_text.size() > 0 && output.unknown.back_route == 'community'.

        The strip's search is one tab row, mine alone, whose q two nested lists read as a case-folded contains: people on search_text, the generated column that is the display name and the handle in one, communities on the name, each hit a link to its page; a blank q draws no panel at all; a q that matches nothing gets each panel's own sentence: output.people.size() == output.expected_people && output.people.all(p, p.display_name.lowerAscii().contains(input.q.lowerAscii()) || p.handle.lowerAscii().contains(input.q.lowerAscii())) && output.people.all(p, p.link.route == 'profile' && p.link.handle == p.handle) && output.communities.size() == output.expected_communities && output.communities.all(c, c.name.lowerAscii().contains(input.q.lowerAscii()) && c.link.route == 'community' && c.link.id == c.id) && output.none.people.size() == 0 && output.none.communities.size() == 0 && output.none.people_text.size() > 0 && output.none.communities_text.size() > 0 && output.blank.panels_hidden && output.strip.has_search.

        Every token the design block declares carries a light and a dark value under the same name in the emitted shell/design.css, and no authored screen or shared stylesheet writes a hex — output.tokens.size() > 0 && output.tokens.all(t, t.light != '' && t.dark != '') && output.authored.all(css, !css.matches('#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}')) — so switching the device appearance re-resolves tokens with no state change and no reload. The driver reads the emitted and the authored files; a fixture in the test's own input could not fail.

        profile

        A profile is one person's header, their about and interests, and exactly their friends: output.header.size() == 1 && output.header[0].handle == input.handle && output.friends.size() == input.friends_seeded && output.friends.all(f, f.user_id == output.header[0].id) && output.neighbour_friends.size() == input.neighbour_friends_seeded — the counts are the demo network's (five for mariana-costa, three for aline-barros), so a filter on the wrong column cannot pass by returning everybody or nobody. The friendship read is one filter on user_id, because the 015 mirror keeps two rows per pair (decision 5).

        A handle nobody carries resolves the header to the empty collection without erroring — output.header == [] && error == null — and the screen says so instead of drawing a blank card.

        Friendship

        Between two people the demo network did not befriend (mariana-costa and andre-carvalho), accepting a request yields exactly two edges, one per direction, and removes both halves in the same transaction: output.edges_before == [] && output.edges.size() == 2 && output.edges.exists(e, e.user_id == input.from_id && e.friend_id == input.to_id) && output.edges.exists(e, e.user_id == input.to_id && e.friend_id == input.from_id) && output.sent == [] && output.inbox == []. A browser insert into friendship is refused because no arm exists for it — output.browser_insert.kind == 'rls_denied' — and deleting one edge removes its mirror: output.edges_after_one_delete == [].

        FriendRequest

        A pending request and an unapproved testimonial reach exactly their two parties and nobody else, on the sync path as on the CRUD path: a third guest's shape over friend_request, friend_request_sent, testimonial_draft or testimonial_pending carries no row — output.friend_request == [] && output.friend_request_sent == [] && output.testimonial_pending == [] && output.testimonial_draft == [] — because every such row is private to one party, and the public testimonial table holds approved rows alone. The regression this catches is the one the architect seat found in this turn's first draft: a public table narrowed in SQL, which PostgREST honours and Electric never sees.

        Asking to befriend oneself is refused at the table CHECK — error.kind == 'check_violation' && output == null — so the control on one's own page cannot produce a row even if it is reached; the own-page frame will hide it in the first place, on the strength of the Me probe.

        FriendRequestSent · FriendRequest · Fan

        Asking inserts one private row taking its asker from the token, and the 015 mirror writes the addressee's half in the same transaction: output.sent.size() == 1 && output.sent[0].from_id == input.from_id && output.inbox.size() == 1 && output.inbox[0].id == output.sent[0].id. Asking twice is refused by the pair's unique, asking a friend or crossing a request already waiting the other way by the 015 guard, and withdrawing deletes both halves: output.again.kind == 'unique_violation' && output.after_withdraw.sent == [] && output.after_withdraw.inbox == [] && output.to_friend.kind == 'check_violation' && output.crossing.kind == 'check_violation'.

        Declining is the addressee deleting their half, and the mirror removes the asker's, so the asker's control returns to "add as friend" without anyone being told why; a third person can neither see nor delete either half: output.inbox == [] && output.sent == [] && output.third_read == [] && output.third_delete.kind == 'rls_denied'.

        Being a fan is one public row taking its fan from the token; the idol's count is a projection over the public rows and moves for the writer on the spot and for everyone else on their next read, Fan being server-durable until the fãs turn makes it live; the count before is read, not assumed, so the demo network may change: output.row.fan_id == input.fan_id && output.idol_count == output.idol_fans_before + 1. A second row for the pair is refused by the unique, oneself as idol by the CHECK, and the row-scoped delete removes mine alone: output.again.kind == 'unique_violation' && output.self.kind == 'check_violation' && output.after_delete.idol_count == output.idol_fans_before.

        Exactly one friend arm is visible for every relation the reader can have with a person — none (ask), asked (request sent), asked by (accept and decline), friends (undo) — none at all on the reader's own page, and the friends tally is one higher on a friend's page than on a stranger's: output.none.visible_arms == ['ask-friend', 'be-fan'] && output.requested.visible_arms == ['withdraw-request', 'be-fan'] && output.pending.visible_arms == ['accept-request', 'decline-request', 'be-fan'] && output.friend.visible_arms == ['unfriend', 'unfan'] && output.friend.friends_count == output.none.friends_count + 1 && output.own.visible_arms == [] && output.own.note.size() > 0. The relation is read through the reader's own Me row (decision 16): mariana-costa reading rafael-lima sees friends, reading andre-carvalho sees ask, reading herself sees the sentence.

        AppUser

        A fresh database already holds a living network: output.people.size() >= 14 && output.people.all(p, output.friendships.exists(f, f.user_id == p.id)) && output.communities.size() >= 10 && output.scraps.size() >= 30 — fourteen people, every one of them with friends, communities with members and forum topics, scraps and approved testimonials between them, so a guest's first screen is never empty (decision 8).

        Decisions

        1. yogurt takes the terminal's door and has no anonymous reader. The original required an invitation and a login before anything; the terminal publishes passkey and guest, and auth.required: true gates every screen. Rejected: a hand-written sign-in with an e-mail field (demanding what the runtime does not offer is a compile error), and a public browse mode (yogurt never had one). Accepted losses: a crawler sees the door; a guest identity lives in sessionStorage and a passkey is what brings a person back to their friends.
        2. Public content with owner writes is public plus additive raw policies, never a declared private widened in SQL. #Access has no "everyone reads, the owner writes" mode, and the browser mirror believes the declared mode; widening in SQL would make one table mean "mine" in the tab and "everyone's" on the server. 011 adds the arms — asker/addressee on FriendRequest, author/owner on Scrap, author/subject on Testimonial, fan, owner, member, author — and two column grants narrow what an UPDATE may touch (handle stays out of reach; a request's and a testimonial's only writable column is its acceptance). Narrowing is always safe under the mirror rule.
        3. Me: a live, private row per person, provisioned synchronously. The binding grammar has no session placeholder, so the only way a screen can ask "is this mine" or "which row is mine" is a table RLS has already narrowed to one row. A trigger inside the auth service's insert (013) rather than a pipeline, because a guest must not wait seconds for their own card to exist; read-only to browsers (012) so nobody deletes themselves out of their own page.
        4. Ownership and state are empty-or-not probes, and every control is a sibling of its probe, never its child. A region nested inside a probe's item template binds against the probe's row; a sibling keeps the enclosing row and is chosen by a :empty sibling combinator. A probe carries no whitespace inside it, since the sweep removes stale elements only and a text node would keep it non-empty forever.
        5. A friendship is two rows, minted by a trigger. One row per direction makes a friends list one filter on user_id with the friend as an embed, and a friends count a projection over that same read; a single undirected row would need an OR over two columns and a template that cannot say which embed is "the other person". 015 mints both edges when the addressee sets accepted and removes the request; deleting either edge removes its mirror. No browser INSERT arm exists on friendship, so the trigger is the only writer. Rejected: a materialized view (not a table, so it would not sync) and a pipeline (seconds of delay for a tap the person is watching).
        6. Pending state is two private rows, one per party, kept equal by triggers — never a public row narrowed in SQL. This turn's first draft declared requests and unapproved testimonials public and replaced their SELECT arm with the two parties' own; the architect seat showed that PostgREST honours that and Electric does not: the sync path reads the WAL, applies no policy, and the auth service mints a shape token for any scoped table, so a third guest could stream every pending row. A row only two people may see must therefore be a row only their scopes carry: the asker's FriendRequestSent and the addressee's FriendRequest, the writer's TestimonialDraft and the subject's TestimonialPending, each private on its party, the second half written only by the 015 mirror (011 revokes its browser INSERT), and the one word each addressee may write — accepted, approved — held by a column grant. Accepting mints the friendship edges; approving inserts the public Testimonial; deleting either half removes the other. Rejected: private with a shared grant table (a third table per flow for the same two scopes), and a pipeline (seconds of delay for a tap the person is watching).
        7. A forum is its members'. A topic or a reply from outside the community is refused by a BEFORE INSERT trigger (017) with the code the screen already reads as a refusal, because RLS cannot express "a row of another table says yes" without a helper, and a policy that reads membership under the writer's own RLS would read the public table anyway. The screen will hide the form behind a membership probe; the trigger is the backstop.
        8. A fresh yogurt comes populated. 020 inserts fifteen fictional people with friendships, scraps, approved testimonials, fans, ratings, twelve communities with members, and fifteen forum threads with replies, as a raw migration with fixed uuids and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A social network with nobody in it cannot be used, let alone judged; a migration rather than seed: because the rows are user-generated content a database holds, and fixed ids because tests and fixtures name them. Every person, place and sentence is invented.
        9. Relationship and category are stored as message keys. {msg[relationship]} renders the row's own value through the reader's catalogue, so "namorando" and "dating" are one stored word, the CEL enum closes the set, and a select control's options are the same keys. Rejected: storing the Portuguese word (untranslatable) and an integer code (a second mapping the screen would have to carry).
        10. The identity is Scrapbook (DESIGN.md): the pale-blue page, white panels with light-blue title bands, blue links, and yogurt's pink spent on commitment alone. Chosen over the 2009 redesign and over a feed-era card stream, because the brief names the artifact and a reader who was there must recognize it in the first second. Both appearances carry the same token names; the dark twin lowers value and keeps hue.
        11. The strip, the back stack, sign-out, the screen states, row motion, the unconfirmed-write badge and the storybook are the terminal's. No screen redraws them; the app dresses the strip in header blue through shell/shared/chrome.css and nothing else, and keeps the guest's strip by offering a passkey (auth.promote): the terminal draws no strip for a guest it offers no way in to, and the brief's name-beside-sign-out needs one.
        12. The first turn is knowingly inert. A fresh guest lands on a card with three zeros, a rail of people, and profiles that offer nothing to do; their own profile is blank with no road to editing yet. That is the plan, not an oversight: the controls arrive on the screens that own them — befriend and fan on perfil (turn 3), scraps (turn 4), requests end to end (turn 5), testimonials (turn 6), communities (turns 7–9), the reader's own form (turn 10) — each as a form over an entity declared here, and the own-profile frame that names what is missing and where to fix it is drawn with the form it points at. Until then the demo network is what sells the next click.
        13. Pictures are links, and a face and a letter are the two states of one box. The cluster carries no blob plane; a person's picture is a URL they supply (photo_url), as a community's is, and capabilities.resources admits image requests to any https host so a reader may paste any link. The demo network's faces are stock portraits by link, its communities' pictures seeded photos by link: a social network with no faces is dead, and faces that only arrive with uploads would have arrived in turn 15; since turn 18 the demo network's own pictures are the app's static files (decision 30), and this decision stands for the picture a reader pastes. Each picture is the row's own photo_url bound into the face's img (the embed carries the column where the row is a join), and a null link binds as the binder's transparent pixel, a data: src that fetches nothing; the letter disc shows exactly when the src is that pixel, so the choice is made by the bound value and never by an image's load: a missing link never draws a broken glyph. In a posed frame the fixture adapter blanks every src to the same pixel, so the storybook shows discs where the live page shows faces. A link whose host is down or blocked still draws a broken image, an accepted risk of pictures by link, named here, and the reason same-origin copies of the demo faces were on the plan and are decision 30. Until turn 13 each picture was a nested one-row region filtered on the link, the disc its :empty, which cost a read per face (thirty-four on a profile) and was replaced once the pixel was known (decision 25). Rejected: AI-generated portraits (a second generator to pin for the faces); same-origin files (deferred: they would make the demo offline-safe, and belong with the richer fake data of turn 18). The demo rows are edited in place rather than by an upgrade migration: 020 is applied by initdb on a fresh volume alone, and no database of this app exists outside a fresh volume yet; the day one does, demo content changes become upgrade migrations like any other (docs/schema-change-admission.md).
        14. The door is the terminal's gate markup dressed as a split page, after roda. The terminal renders the gate — intro, name, hint, error, passkey, guest, providers — and ships no style; the app's shared stylesheet is on that page too, so it lays the intro and the form out as a header-blue panel beside the form on the pale ground, with the panel's question and its line as the page's own words per language, since no catalogue reaches the gate. The alternative, a login screen of the app's own, is refused by the prelude (the terminal owns sign-in); the default gate, unstyled, is a door that does not say what is behind it.
        15. A reader's relation to a person is read through the reader's own row. Friendship and Fan are public, as their lists were, so a probe filtered on the person's id answers "does anyone" rather than "do I", and the binding grammar carries no session placeholder. The one row that is mine alone is Me: the person row nests a one-row me region, and inside it the friendship and fan probes filter on {id} (mine) and {param.handle} (theirs, through an inner embed, so the read is server-computed). The forms that start a relation need the person's id, so they stay siblings in the person row, and :has() on the arms box joins what the probes know to which form is drawn. The forms that undo one live inside the probe row they undo: a filtered delete resolves its rows against the public table before the policy narrows it, so idol_id=eq.{id} on a person with other fans lands on another fan's row and deletes nothing (found in the turn-4 playtest). The two request halves are private to one party each and need no detour. Rejected: a per-reader derived table (a pipeline round trip for a tap the person is watching) and making friendship private (its list is public on every profile). Accepted and recorded: a decline is silent and the asker may ask again without limit, as the original allowed; a cooldown is a row nobody asked for yet.
        16. The scrapbook is its own page; the profile teases it. The box to leave a scrap lives on scrapbook, above the list, and the profile's scraps panel is the newest three with the count and two links — the band's to read on, the foot's to the box — as the 2004 tab was, and because a profile with a textarea in it is a form, not a page. Newest first, because a scrapbook is read from the top for what is new and the old is scrolled to, not for. Who may delete is the 011 policy's OR — the writer, or the owner of the page — and the control is drawn for them alone by two one-row probes on the reader's Me row in each scrap's row, one on author_id and one on owner_id: the ownership primitive (decision 4) applied twice, no session placeholder, no derived column. Deleting takes two taps, the same arm-and-commit as unfriend, because a scrap is as gone as a friendship. A person may scrap their own page, as they could then; the demo network happens to hold none. The reply road is "responder" under every scrap, to the writer's own scrapbook, which is where the conversation lived. A scrap is never edited; it was not then, and an edit would need an updated_at the brief does not ask for. Accepted: no paging; the page is one list however long, and the demo's longest scrapbook is five; the first scrapbook past fifty earns a "mais" that this list's limit already knows how to grow. Rejected: a can_delete computed on the server (a round trip per row for a glance the client already has the rows for); the box on the profile (every profile visit would mount a form); hiding "apagar…" until hover (a phone has no hover). Scrap stays server, with the cost the sprint wrap named: a scrap reaches another reader's open scrapbook or início on their next read, and a writer whose scrap the owner swept meanwhile gets the refusal line on "apagar"; it has the network's highest write rate, which is what a live shape would carry to every tab.
        17. The three relation tables are live, and a relation is read as my own rows, each probing the page's person. A server region re-reads after this client's own write to its entity and never otherwise, so the friendship rows the 015 trigger mints on an accept were invisible to the accepter until a reload, and the asker's "pedido enviado" outlived a decline. Friendship, FriendRequestSent and FriendRequest now ride the sync shape: the public one reaches everybody (its list was public already), the private halves reach their one party, as Me does. The probes also change shape: a read whose filter or select goes through an embed (friend.handle=eq., a !fk hint) is routed to PostgREST; on a live table it does update, by re-reading on every change to the table anywhere in the network, and its rows never enter the local collection, so a row-scoped write on one of them finds nothing to write (início's "recusar" said so in the playtest). So each relation is a list of my own rows with no embed — my friendships, my sent requests, my inbox — served from the collection, and every row nests a one-row probe on AppUser filtered on that row's other party and the route's handle; :has() over the probe picks the row that is this page's, and that row carries its own undo, row-scoped. Cost: the friendship collection is lazy, so a client loads the rows its views ask for, but every client receives every friendship change in the network from the moment a page opens, so the term that grows is the network's write rate times open tabs, not the table; and each probe is one PostgREST read of a server row at mount, so a reader with N friends spends N reads on a profile and the arms hold until the last lands.
