The same rule reaches forward: the three testimonial tables and Fan are server today, and an approval or a fan written on one row and mirrored or counted on another will show its mirror on the next read only, so the turns that build depoimentos and fãs make those tables live and read their probes as my rows with a person probe, in the same edit as the screen. The tile lists that keep an embed (friends, the profile's amigos, início's friends) are read-only and re-read on any profile edit in the network; the price of a name beside a face until the select parser takes a hint. The pair unique is ordered, so a request to a friend or across one already waiting the other way is refused by a 015 guard, and an accept clears the reverse pair too. Início's pending panel is the same inbox list without the probe, and it carries no embed: a region read with an embed comes through PostgREST, and a live table's row that arrived that way is not in the collection a row-scoped write resolves against, so its "recusar" found no row to delete (seen in the playtest, fixed by reading the asker through a nested region on their own key); it sits under the reader's card because an unanswered request is the one thing on início that asks something of the reader, and it shows its sentence when empty so the place is learned before it is needed. There is no "sent requests" panel: what I asked for is read on each person's page, as it was. A withdrawn request leaves the panel under the reader's finger, because the half is live and there is nothing left to answer. The profile shows twelve friends and início nine: one row of tiles more where the page is the person's. Friends are newest first on both, with no sort to choose; the original had none either. The strip carries no pending count: notifications are outside the brief. Rejected: polling a server region (a clock for a fact the shape already carries); keeping the embed filter and refreshing on a timer.
        18. The directory is ten sections, the search is a row, the create form is on the page. A category is a message key on the row (decision 9), so browsing by category is ten public reads filtered on a word, in the order the 2004 directory listed them, and a category with no community draws nothing rather than an empty band. The search box is relational like everything else: one tab row per browser tab, upserted by the form, with the results region nested in it reading name=ilike.*{q}*, a snapshot read that re-runs when the row changes; the results panel is hidden by an attribute bound to q, so a blank search draws nothing. Creating a community is a form on the directory and not a page of its own, because the 2004 form was three fields and the new row's home is the section it lands in. Accepted: no paging per section (the demo's largest category holds three; a section past fifty earns a limit and a "mais"); search submits on a tap, not on each keystroke (a keystroke search is a machine and a round trip per letter for a list this size). Rejected: a route parameter for the search (a search is not an address anyone keeps); a category filter as a route (ten routes for one read each); a picture field on the create form (it belongs to the community's own page, where the owner edits it). Also decided: a second community with the same name is allowed, as the original allowed its thousand "Eu odeio acordar cedo"; the hits are capped at twenty with no "mais" until a search returns more than that in the demo, which none does; a search of spaces or of a wildcard (%, *) lists what it matches, on a public list, and is not worth a handler; this box is the directory's own filter and Buscar (a later turn) is the global search over people and communities; "my communities" stays on início, where it already is; every community name is a link to its page, and a category lists newest first, so the community a reader just made is the first row of its section, one tap from the page it made; a create form cannot navigate to a row whose id the client minted after the tap, which is why the creator is not carried there. The search folds case and not accents: "cafe" misses "café", as the original did; an unaccented search column is a generated column the brief does not ask for yet. Cost, as the architect seat simulated it: the ten section reads coalesce into one request and the member counts into another, but each row's picture read repeats its photo_url key and so does not coalesce, one request per community on every screen that draws faces; the blank search still reads its twenty hidden rows. Two seams for the platform's pending list: the coalescer could keep repeated non-equality keys, and the category word lives in the CEL, the form's options, ten filters and ten option values with only the CHECK enforcing it, which a lint over equality filters and option values would catch.
        19. Membership is read through the me row; the forum's form is drawn for members and guarded for everyone. Membership is public, as the member lists were, so "am I a member" is the same detour the profile takes (decision 16): a probe nested in my Me row filtered on my id and the route's id, no embed, and the leave form row-scoped inside the probe's row. The new-topic form is drawn only when that probe has a row, which is a courtesy and not a rule: the rule is the 017 guard (decision 7), which refuses a non-member's insert with the code the form already paints as a refusal, so a hand-made request meets the same wall as a hidden form. Leaving was two taps until turn 11 and is one, since rejoining is free (decision 23). The owner may leave; the community stays, owned, with no members, as the original allowed, and nothing here deletes a community, and 011 grants no delete arm on it, since a delete would cascade through every member's topics and posts: an ownerless-of-members community is accepted until a moderation turn, and the demo holds none. Editing a community — its description, its picture — is the owner's and arrives with the editing turn beside editar perfil; no topic is deleted or moderated yet. Members are capped at twelve with the count in the band and a members page since turn 11 (decision 23); topics are newest first with no paging, the demo's largest forum holding two; a topic's page, where replies live, is topic, and every title links there. Rejected: a derived "member" column on the community row (a pipeline round trip for a probe the row already answers); hiding the forum from non-members (the forum was public reading). Two things the record states rather than fixes: the armed leave is ephemeral, a details the next paint closes, so a reload lands on "sair da comunidade…" with nothing deleted; and the members and the count are server-durable, so another reader's join reaches an open page on its next read, not live, which is the trade the profile's counts make too.
        20. The route carries the community so the probe can; replies are the writer's to delete, and nobody's to edit. A membership probe nested in the reader's Me row can filter only on its own columns and the route's params, so the thread's address is /comunidade/:community/topico/:id: the community's id rides in the route, the probe reads {param.community}, and a title's link carries both ids. Only the first segment translates, through the community's own slug, as the address reads as a path under the community. Replies are oldest first, because a thread is read top-down and the box sits at its foot, where the next reply goes. A reply is the writer's to delete in two taps, as a scrap is, and nobody's to edit; the topic itself has no delete arm in 011 since the sprint 3 wrap, as the community has none: a delete cascades through every member's replies, which are theirs; the opener deletes a topic with no replies through 022's guard (decision 25), and a moderation turn decides the rest. The topic's community is read through an embed in the select, which routes the one-row read through PostgREST; it is a name beside a title and never written to, so the cost is a read on every change to topics, which is what the forum's own list already pays. Accepted: no paging of replies, the demo's longest thread holding four; Post stays server-durable, so another reader's reply reaches an open thread on its next read, as the forum's list does, the live tables being the three relation tables alone. Rejected: a membership column on the topic row (a derived fact for a probe the me row answers); a flat route /topico/:id with the community read from the row (the probe cannot read a sibling region's column).
        21. A testimonial is a friend's word, one per person, approved before it is seen; the three tables go live. The 2004 product had it so: only a friend could write one, you approved it before it appeared, and one per friend was the norm. The 021 guard holds the friend rule and the no-second-after-approval half where a hand-made request meets them, with the same SQLSTATE as the row CHECK; a unique pair on the draft and on the public table holds one-per-person under concurrency, where a guard's read cannot; the invariant from turn 1 refuses oneself; and an unfriend takes the unapproved ones with it in 015, since the rule is a friend's word. The guard runs as the caller: its reads are public tables and the caller's own drafts, and a definer would answer a stranger's hand-made insert naming another writer with a sentence that reveals a private draft, so 011 also stops granting author_id and from_id, which default to the token and which no form sends. The pending state stays two private rows kept equal by 015 (decision 6), and the three tables become live for the same reason the request halves did in turn 6: the subject's copy and the public row are a trigger's rows, and a server-durable region re-reads only after this client's own write, so without live the subject would reload to see a draft arrive and the writer to see the approval. Because they are live, no list here carries an embed: a row that arrives through an embed-path read is not in the collection a row-scoped write resolves against (decision 16), and every row on this page carries a form. The writer is therefore a nested region on their own key, the início pedidos idiom. The profile's teaser reads the same way. The communities panel sits under the portrait, where the original kept it, and reads Membership with an embed, which is safe there: server-durable and form-free. Início gains one line, not a panel: an approval is a decision about a sentence and belongs on the page that shows the sentence, so the line counts and links. Accepted: no paging; the writer may not edit a draft, since 011 revokes UPDATE so the subject never approves text the writer no longer shows; a withdrawn or discarded one is gone, not kept. Rejected: approving from início (two places to do one thing); a testimonial without friendship (the original's rule, and the guard is four lines); an embed on a live list (the turn-6 lesson).
        22. Editing is a form over the row that is already mine; leaving a community is one tap; members get a page, not a longer panel. The profile's edit form is the ownership primitive once more: my app_user row read through my me row, every control bound to its column with data-value, one row-scoped update, and 011's column grant the only rule, so the page needs no own-page probe and nobody edits anyone else's. The handle is not edited: it is the address of every page about me and the name every row that points at me carries, and a rename is a moderation turn's question. The same primitive edits a community: a Me probe on owner_id draws the form in the owner's page and the owner's policy admits the write, description and photo link alone, since the name is the community's address in the directory and the category decides its section. Leaving a community is one tap, by DESIGN.md's rule: two taps where getting back needs someone else's yes (unfriend) or where writing is destroyed (apagar), one where the reader can redo it alone, and rejoining is free; turn 8 made it two and recorded that this turn would make it one. A members page behind the count, not a longer panel, because the panel's twelve are a tease and a list of hundreds is a page of its own, the shape amigos already has; it reads Membership with an embed, safe there since it is server-durable and form-free. The strip already names the reader and leads to their page (decision 13), so the brief's "own-name link" was there since turn 1. A control the reader empties submits the empty string, which an optional column must not hold and the https rule refuses, so every optional control names the editing-text adapter, golaberto's, whose parse is trim-or-null: a cleared field is an unset column, on the date too, whose client normaliser refuses "". A seam the walk met: inside an item, a route link with no params and no other bound attribute is skipped before the pass that addresses links, since only elements with a bound attribute are visited, and the static pass never sees a template's contents; the two "editar perfil →" links bind their title so the pass reaches them. Recorded for the harvest. Accepted: no picture upload, pictures stay links (decision 9); no "saved" sentence, the row re-reading with my words being the confirmation. Rejected: editing inline on the profile (one page, two modes, every rule doubled); a rename of the handle; an owner deleting a community (decision 20 stands).
        23. One box in the strip, two lists under it, the directory's idiom. The 2004 top bar had one search that found people and communities; so does the strip here, on its own page, since the strip's own markup is the terminal's and holds no form. The page is the directory's search again: a tab row the form upserts, its q read by nested lists, the attribute bound to it hiding the panels while blank. People match on search_text, a generated column that is the display name and the username in one, because a person without a name is their username everywhere here and a second list would show the same person twice, and because an or filter is PostgREST's alone: the local matcher that serves a posed fixture has no or, while one ilike on one column it serves on both sides; a comma or a parenthesis typed into an or group would also have split it. The column is not named search_name, which the local matcher would fold for accents while the server's ilike does not, so a fixture would pass a query the live app fails; case folds on both sides, accents on neither, until the server carries a collation that folds them, which the edge's PGlite cannot yet; communities match on the name alone, since the description is prose. Both are a case-folded contains, ASCII case, as the directory's is; neither ranks. Accepted: no paging, one cap of twenty-four on each list, four rows of six tiles and as many rows, with the hint saying so and asking for a longer word when someone is missing, since by name the same early names always win a short query; the demo holds fifteen people and twelve communities, under the cap; no search of topics or scraps, which a search of posts would need a text index for. Rejected: a search box inside the strip (not the app's markup); separate people and community pages (one gesture, two answers); ranking (nothing here is ranked).
        24. The debts: paid in the mechanisms that owed them. A community's creator is its first member because the create path's trigger (022) mints the membership, not because a screen remembers to. The opener deletes a topic through a DELETE arm behind a guard that refuses while a reply exists, the opener's own included, so the control the reply count hides is never the rule, and across readers that count is as fresh as the page's last read, since post is a server table; the guard is a trigger, not a policy clause, because it runs after the row is locked and so sees a reply that committed first, and it lets a cascade through (one trigger level deeper) so 005's meaning for a leaving person or community is kept. Its refusal sentence is generic, since the control is hidden while replies exist and a failed delete is then more likely the network's. A face box binds its own row's picture, the embed carrying photo_url, instead of a nested read per face: thirty-three regions gone and the reads they cost with them (decision 14 holds the mechanism); 011 is kept byte for byte although its comment points forward to 022, because the edge's ledger refuses a shipped script that changed; a null link binds as the binder's transparent pixel, a data: src that fetches nothing, and the letter disc keys on it. The nested one-row reads of a person that stay are each a row the screen does not hold: início's own card and the asker in its requests; the writer in the profile's testimonial teaser and in the testimonials page's waiting and approved lists; the community page's owner; the edit form's own row. Each is a live list that carries no embed, or the screen's own subject, and the face binds from that row once it is read; the person probes beside them are probes, not reads of a face. A count is one ICU message whose plural the interpreter picks, so "1 amigo" needs no handler. "salvo" is the screen's own success stamp.
        25. Fãs: the toggle on the profile, a stateless "ser fã" under every tile, the list behind the count. A fan row is public and its state for the reader is a probe on two keys, the person's and the reader's, and a binding resolves against its enclosing row alone: inside a tile the reader's id is a row away, so "am I a fan" cannot be asked per tile without a read per tile, the cost turn 13 just removed. So the tile carries the create and no state: one tap makes the reader a fan, "você é fã", a link to the profile where the one-tap undo lives, shows under the tile for a breath by the saved line's mechanism (the screen's success stamp, held by a delayed transition in the form that keeps focus, which a browser that does not focus a tapped button never grants: the one known hole, the terminal's to close), and the count moves where one is shown; a second tap is refused by the unique pair and the line in the tile says so while the screen holds the refusal, clearing with it, since nothing in the tile types; the reader's own tile hides it through the me probe, which is local. The tile is where a person "appears": people to meet, search, a friends list, a fan list, a community's members and the members page. Not the two panels of the reader's own circle on início (their friends, their fans), which are theirs to visit rather than to court, and not rows: a scrap, a testimonial or a reply carries its writer as a link and its own gestures, and a courting button there would compete with them. A fan of mine on my fans page still gets the button, since being a fan of a fan is the point. Undo is the profile's one tap. The toggle with its state stays on the profile, where the route's handle reaches the probe. The list is the friends page over fan rows, newest first, the fan as an embed on fan_id; início shows the reader's own fans the way it shows their friends. Rejected: a probe per tile through an inner embed on me (no key joins me to fan); fan as a live table so the probe is local (still two keys from one row); a handler (none, by decision 10). Decision 28 later proved a reader-relative policy as a fourth shape; it does not serve here, since the fans page needs everyone's rows and a second table of "mine" is the read per tile this decision declined.
        26. Karma: the rating is the rater's private row, the smileys are the cluster's derived row. A rating is three levels, trustworthy, cool and sexy, zero to three, one row per rater per friend, private to the rater (decision 2): on a friend's profile the reader reads their own row for that person on the friendship row's key, the update form lives in that row, and the create form beside it is drawn only once the region has stamped that there is none. The levels cross a value adapter as numbers. The smileys everyone sees are the rounded mean of every rater's row and how many rated, which no reader's own rows can supply, so the cluster keeps them: one KarmaSmiley row per rated person, public and live, written by a definer trigger on karma and by nothing a browser holds (023 takes back the standing grants); live because trigger-born rows reach a server region only on its own client's next write (decision 4), and a rating must move the smileys at once. The level a screen draws is a message key the row carries, the {msg[col]} idiom, so a glyph is the catalogue's. The row exists from three raters up, by the refresh itself and not by a screen's filter: with one, the public row would be that one friend's exact vote; with two, a rater who knows their own levels could solve for the other; from three the row is a mean, and what remains (a live change the rated person can date, the count moving by one) is accepted and named here, as orkut's was. Only a friend rates, by a guard on the row, a rating leaves with the friendship, and a rating is undone in one tap, by DESIGN's redo clause: the three levels are the reader's to enter again. The refresh is callable by the trigger alone: PostgREST publishes every function at /rpc with EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default, and 023 takes that back for this one and, by the global default (a per-schema default undoes only a per-schema grant), for every function after it. The residual the sprint's architect named is larger than three raters hides: a rater who steps their own level through 0 to 3 and watches the public mean flip learns the other raters' sum, and an unfriend's drop in the count dates the leaving friend's vote. That is accepted as the price of a live mean, named here and left: the sprint 5 architect measured that a refresh on the ticker would not close the stepping channel at any cadence nor the count's drop, and a floor of five with hysteresis would only blur them; the residual stands as the design's. Rejected: a view over karma (the program declares tables, and a view would be a second grammar for one read); the mean computed by the client (it cannot see the rows); a pipeline box for one aggregate a trigger keeps exactly.
        27. Novidades: a feed table the cluster writes, read under a reader-relative policy. The brief decided a view unioning three public tables; the program declares tables and has no view grammar, and turn 15 proved the shape that does the same work: a Feed row per public doing, written by definer triggers on scrap, testimonial and membership as each happens and removed with its source, backfilled once. What makes it the reader's is the policy 024 restates on the table: a row is visible when its actor is the reader's friend, so one server region on início with no filter but a cap reads exactly their friends' twenty newest doings. Server, not live: a reader-relative policy is no shape to sync, and the brief wants the panel fresh when início opens, not pushed. The sentence per kind is a message the row names by key, and the kind as a data attribute picks which link follows it, so three kinds are one row template. Nothing private enters: no draft, no request, no rating, and a testimonial is dated by the day it was written, since its approval lives only in the subject's private row; the cost is that one approved late sits under newer doings and, past twenty, out of reach, which "ver mais" in sprint 5 answers. The policy reads O(feed) for a reader whose friends did little; a fan-out inbox or an index by actor and time is the shape to revisit before the table nears a hundred thousand rows. Rejected: the view (no grammar; a second mechanism beside 27's); three regions, one per table, merged by the stylesheet (no order across them); a live table (the policy is per reader). Measured on the edge at the sprint 5 wrap: novidades is empty there for every reader. The edge serves a GET on a public-scope table as a shared read with no subject (isPublicRead, scopes public: alone), so auth_uid() is null inside the reader-relative policy and nothing passes it; the local stack's PostgREST always carries the subject, which is why the ledger driver and the walk passed. On the edge, visibility is a scope, not a policy: a row a reader may see must carry that reader's scope. The feed is the inbox now, shipped at the wrap: FeedItem, one row per reader and doing under user:<reader>, fanned out by 025 from the log for each friend of the actor as a doing lands, and for a new friendship the friend's hundred newest, removed with the doing and with the friendship; the log itself is the cluster's alone, and the screens read the inbox newest first. It answers the scale question too: a sparse reader's read is bounded by their own rows. The release's verify runs a feed journey first, a friend's scrap read on início and on the page, so the edge cannot go green again with novidades empty.
        28. Polish is paid in the grammar the app already has. "Ver mais" past the twenty novidades is a page, news, the panel's row over the same policy with a cap of a hundred, because a cap that grows needs arithmetic no attribute has and a second route needs nothing. "Para você" is a me probe on the doing's subject, local and free, and a rule that swaps the name for the word. The arms under a row of tiles sit level because a name is always two lines tall, and each is the control height. The interests panel of a person who filled nothing is gone by a rule on its own empty cells; "responder" on one's own scrap by the writer's probe the row already carried. What polish did not get: a "saved" word that does not depend on the tapped button keeping focus, which is the terminal's stamp to give (on the pending list), and tap-to-set karma rows, which a radio group through a value adapter has not been proven to carry and stays with sprint 5's driver turn. What still depends on the tapped button keeping focus, after this turn: the "ser fã" arm under a tile and the "salvo" of the two edit forms; the rating's form confirms by showing the reader's own levels, focus or not. The arm's height is the design's control height, 36 px, under the 44 px floor some guides name and above the 24 px one the visual gate holds. The scrapbook frames that drew relative times now draw the datetime format, and every declared state has its frame, which lint holds.
        29. The demo network's pictures are the app's own files, content-addressed, served as statics on every target. Decision 14 took pictures by link and named the risk: a host down or blocked draws a broken image, and the demo faces sat on two hosts the site did not own; the sprint 4 walk saw a letter where a picture should be. They are twenty-five files under pictures/ now, named by their sha256, three hundred and eighty kilobytes in the tree, declared as cluster statics the way doom declares its engine, so caddy serves /pictures/<file> on the local stack and the docker release and the edge bundle writes the same files into its assets: one meaning on three targets, offline, cached by content. The picture rule admits that exact shape beside https, a 64-hex name with its extension, so a reader cannot point a face at any other path; their own picture is still a link they paste (decision 14 stands for them). assets/manifest.json records each file's source, author and license, which the credits screen draws, since ten of them are Wikimedia Commons files under CC BY and BY-SA terms. A fifteenth person joins the network with her own scraps, a topic and friends, so the rail's cap and the newest-member states have a row beyond the fourteen, and the older threads gain a quiet topic, old scraps and a stranger's reply. Rejected, after the turn's architect: a blob seed from a public bucket (apexrun's shape), which turns on an open blob plane nobody writes, fetches at every launch and integrate, needs a bucket grant, and serves nothing on the docker target; data URIs in the seed (a migration the edge's ledger would carry forever); leaving the links.
        30. The ledger's unreachable clauses are decided by a driver at every integrate, by screen tests over posed rows, and by the release's browser journeys; the karma levels are tap-to-set rows. The sprint 4 walk passed thirteen ids short of a clause no walk reaches: a forged write only a crafted request makes, a race only two sessions run, a cap the fifteen demo people cannot fill, a mean that needs three raters. Three instruments, each at the cheapest tier that can decide its clause. tests/ledger.ts is a build check, so it runs in the integrate closure against the runner's own stack with five guest sessions over /crud: a stranger's delete and a non-owner's update come back as nothing touched (the policy filters, the request succeeds), an outsider's reply, a blank body, a rating by a non-friend or of oneself, a second testimonial and a delete of a replied topic come back refused (a trigger or a CHECK raises), and the delete racing the reply is fired twenty times in both orders and never takes a reply with it. Those rounds are a smoke, not the proof: HTTP cannot pin an interleaving. The proof is at the SQL tier, in the lock order the turn's architect forced with two sessions and pg_sleep on a throwaway database: the row is locked before a BEFORE ROW trigger fires, the reply's foreign key holds the topic's key until the reply commits, and the volatile guard snapshots after the lock, so either the reply fails on a topic gone (017's refusal, or the key's) or the delete fails on a reply landed; the same guard written as a DELETE policy reads before the lock and loses, which is why 022 is a trigger (its comment pins VOLATILE). Each clause is a test step named by its acceptance id, so a failure reports per clause and the later ones still run. tests/screens.test.ts mounts the emitted screens on posed rows for what a photograph cannot judge and the demo cannot reach: the plural counts, the search cap, the saved stamp, and, off the shells, every capped region's limit and the karma rows' shape; the tap itself is a release journey, two guests made friends and a rating given through the chips. The guest strip at phone width, the saved word and the chips are judged by tests/verify.ts, the browser journeys every release is verified with, because the build check's runner image has no browser (recorded for the platform). The karma form draws each smiley as a row of four radio chips; the update form has no button, so a tap on a level is the save, the terminal submitting a buttonless form on change; the first rating keeps "avaliar" since it takes all three. The control vocabulary has no radio, so the program says select, its nearest word. Rejected: the three browser lines as a build check (no browser in the runner); the caps as seeded demo rows (a hundred-person network for a twelve-tile cap); mounting início and the profile whole for the caps and the rows, which the harness's select grammar refuses for an embed hinted by its foreign key column, as the feed's actor and the fan probe's idol are (recorded for the platform).
        31. Escape hatches: none. Argued, not assumed. Everything here is schema, policy, trigger or screen markup: nineteen entities, twenty raw migrations (a declared seam, checked-in SQL a reviewer reads), fourteen screens and zero handlers. The emitted bayt.cue redeclares the cluster unchanged, which is what "none" has to mean to be checkable.

        Team review

        The virtual team's work product: one data-kind="review" section per seat of the studio team named in the head's pronto-team, each carrying the seat's verdict and findings and every finding's disposition. Reviews are outside the ir↔program bijection.

        Sprint 5

        Turn 17 collected the polish, turn 18 shipped the pictures and a fifteenth person, turn 19 built the driver, turn 20 wrote the README and shipped the third edge release; the seats read what each left. The wrap's walk and two reviews come first and read across the four.

        walk · sprint 5 review

        Verdict: approved. The whole ledger, 74 ids, in one pass in file order, two walkers with two guests each on one stack and every count against a crud read: 70 pass outright, 1 fail, 3 pass short of one clause beyond the walk's reach.

        • medium — accept-saved-line: "salvo" showed with the right text, in the success window, with the button focused, and sat beside the button on the same row, not under it, in the edit and community forms at both widths; their foot is a flex row and the karma form's line was the only one under its control. Disposition: fixed — the saved line takes the full row under the button in both feet.
        • medium — the three short clauses: the passkey half of sign-in, which waits for a virtual authenticator in the walk (walker B drove one through CDP once, and the strip named the holder); the search cap of twenty-four, which sixteen people cannot reach and tests/screens.test.ts decides over twenty-six posed rows; the pictures "on the docker release and the edge alike", where the appliance does not bake and the edge was checked by verify. Disposition: recorded — in the brief's "After twenty turns"; the search cap and the edge half are decided by their instruments.
        • low — a legal fifty-two-character name wrapped to five lines on a tile and dropped its "ser fã" arm sixty-eight pixels below its neighbour's. Disposition: fixed — a tile's name clamps to two lines; the whole name is on the profile.
        • low — liveness is split by durability: a request, an acceptance and a pending testimonial reach the other person's open page; a reply, a scrap or a doing written by another person shows on the next read (decision-live-relations, decision-news say so); on the edge even a live row written by another session shows on a later load, seconds after the write. Disposition: recorded — the design as decided for the server tables; the edge's latency is under the architecture line and in the brief.
        • low — a one-frame "1 amigo0 amigos" when a count empties, the stale item and the empty sentence drawn together; a momentary stale smiley row beside "poucas avaliações ainda" after an undo; a pasted picture link that does not resolve draws a broken image box where the letter should fall through; the hidden search panels pre-draw twenty-four tiles at a blank query; one unreproduced forty-three-row novidades read. Disposition: recorded — the count's empty-sentence timing and the picture fall-through are the terminal's (pending list); the pre-drawn panels are the blank query's `**`, a region that should not read at all; the novidades read was not seen again in five tries.

        product · sprint 5 review

        Verdict: request changes, from the files and from the live release played as two guests this seat minted (an English browser at / and a Portuguese one at ?lang=pt-BR, 1280 px and 390 px, the dark twin). The four slices are there as a reader feels them: the polish is paid where the walk said it owed, the faces are yogurt's own and the fifteenth person has a page worth reading, the ledger's unreachable clauses have an instrument each, and the README is the right first page: what the thing is, the shape it exercises, the three instruments, the verbs. What the sprint did not see is on the release itself: on v0.3.0 a friend's doing never reaches the feed, which no journey looks at; and the list after twenty turns overstates the one edge defect it names and misses the two the walk recorded.

        1. blocker — on the live site the novidades never fill. Two guests made friends through the door (request on B's profile, accept on B's início); B left a scrap on Mariana Costa's page and joined Flamengo; A's início kept "Nothing yet" on the open page and after a reload, /en/news drew its empty line, and /crud/feed read as A answers [] for B as actor while friendship holds both rows (A→B at 03:09:42, B→A). The scrap is in the network panel and Flamengo counts six, so the sources landed; the feed row did not, or the reader-relative policy hides it on the edge's database. tests/ledger.ts:200 decides accept-news at integrate against the runner's Postgres and passes; tests/verify.ts has no feed journey, so the third release went green with sprint 4's headline slice and turn 17's "ver mais" page empty for every reader of the real site. The first thing the next sprint takes: a release journey that makes two guests friends, leaves a scrap and reads the row on início; then the edge's cause (024's definer triggers, or its policy, on the edge's database). Disposition: fixed in the wrap — measured and confirmed over the API (the edge serves a public table's GET as a shared read with no subject, so the feed's reader-relative policy passed nothing there); the feed is the inbox now, FeedItem under each reader's scope, fanned out by 025, and the release's verify runs a feed journey first, a friend's scrap read on início and on the page; the platform seam is harvested (llms.txt 7.19, PENDING under Access)
        2. major — "After twenty turns" is not yet the honest list. It says the edge's live tables learn a row on a later load, "so the live-accept clause holds on the edge only across a reload". Measured on the live site today, without a reload on either side: A's request reached B's open início as "quer ser seu amigo" with aceitar and recusar; B's accept turned A's open page of B to "you are friends", "1 friend", the rating form and the friends tile inside the 30-second wait; B's unfriend took A's open início to "0 friends" and the empty sentence inside a second. What tests/verify.ts:150 works around with its reload loop is a lag on the first draw, not a reload-only edge, and the brief should say what was measured. The list also leaves out the two things the walk saw a reader feel, a pasted picture that does not resolve drawing a broken image and the feed and scraps panels not live while a page is open (the next two findings), and it cannot yet know the first finding. Disposition: fixed — the open list says what was measured: the edge's first draw after another session's write can miss the row for seconds while the live update itself arrives on an open page; the broken pasted picture and the panels that are not live by decision are on the list.
        3. medium — a pasted picture link that does not resolve draws the browser's broken-image glyph, never the letter. Played as A: the edit form took https://example.invalid/sem-foto.jpg and said saved; the profile then draws a 160 × 160 frame with the broken glyph in its corner and no "V". accept-photos says "a person without one wears their letter, never a broken image", and decision 14 keys the letter on the binder's pixel, which a dead link is not. A dead link is the common case the 2004 site met daily: a host gone, a hotlink refused. The cheapest shape without a handler is the image's alt as the person's initial inside the disc's styling, so a failed load reads as the letter; the honest alternative is to say in the ledger line that a dead link is the reader's to fix. Disposition: recorded — decision 14 keys the letter on the binder's transparent pixel for a null src; a link that resolves to nothing is a different case, an onerror fall-through the terminal would own; in the brief's open list.
        4. medium — início is live in one panel and not the next, and nothing tells the reader which. B's scrap for Mariana took none of 30 seconds to reach A's open início, in the network panel or the news; a reload drew it in the network panel at once. Decision-live-relations splits liveness by durability, which is the right cost argument, but the felt split is "a friend request arrives on the spot, a friend's scrap does not until I come back". The return-tomorrow moment is fine; the left-open moment is not. The architecture line should decide the feed and the scraps rail as live shapes (Electric applies no policy, so the feed's reader-relative read is the obstacle to name) or início re-reading its server panels when the page regains focus, and the brief should say which panels are live today. Disposition: recorded — the design as decided (decision-live-relations, decision-news: live for the relations, a read on arrival for the server tables); the brief now says the panels should be named one by one, and the architecture line keeps the question of a re-read on focus.
        5. medium — the first moment speaks three ways for an English browser. At / the door draws the Portuguese question and hint ("quem você conhece?", "Entre com a chave do seu aparelho, ou como visitante.") with two English buttons ("Sign in with a passkey", "Continue as guest") and an English accessible description, and the guest click lands on /en, the English catalogue; at ?lang=pt-BR the door is all Portuguese. The app's pt-BR-first default, the terminal's navigator.language and the route's catalogue each decide alone. accept-door says the door is yogurt's; one language decision at the door, the inside following it, is what the ledger line already promises. Disposition: recorded — the door is the terminal's gate and the app dressed it in CSS content that cannot be localised; one language at the door is the terminal's pending item (harvested); in the brief's open list.
        6. medium — the ir's overview is turn 1's framing after twenty turns: "This turn knowingly builds an inert first screen pair (decision 13): the model and two read-only screens … the controls arrive on the screens that own them in the turns that follow", "eight server tables and the live Friendship" where the program carries nineteen entities, eight of them live, and the diagram's "Testimonial -. a later turn's screens .-> profile". The first page of the application design is where a reader starts; it should describe the application as it is, with the decisions the overview cites kept and the turn's voice gone. Disposition: fixed — the overview speaks for the app as it is after twenty turns: nineteen entities, eight live, the derived rows the cluster writes, the three instruments; the diagram's caption no longer promises later turns.
        7. low — "people to meet" never shows the fifteenth person. The rail's cap of fourteen in seed order cuts Letícia Andrade, the one newcomer with a story, so a fresh guest meets the founders and never the person who joined twelve days ago. Newest first, or newest last with the rail reversed, is the product answer; today the cap bites the wrong end. Disposition: recorded — the rail reads the oldest fourteen by decision (the founders lead); the fifteenth is one tile past the cap, which is the cap doing its job; a "newest members" rail is a slice for another sprint.
        8. low — a guest without a name has no heading: their profile's tab reads "yogurt" and the page starts with "guest-35011628" as plain text where a named person has an h1. The handle should be the heading when the name is empty, as the strip and the tiles already do. Beside it, a guest's strip offers two passkey buttons ("sign in with a passkey", "create a passkey") where accept-signin-home says a guest is offered a passkey; at 390 px the second is past the edge, which the one-line clause allows and the reader does not see. Measured for the record: no leaf text on início's dark twin below AA, the tile arms 69 × 36 px, the people rail fourteen tiles. Disposition: recorded — the profile fillers ("didn't say" twice, "lives in —", the count spacing, the birthday format in English, the small link, the skip link) are polish for the next sprint's first slice.

        What the next sprint takes first, in this order: the feed on the edge with a journey that would have caught it; a dead picture link as the letter; one language at the door; the overview rewritten; then the architecture line as the brief has it, the feed at scale before the feed is live.

        architect · sprint 5 review

        Verdict: approve with findings, from the files across the four turns and a throwaway Postgres 18 built from the app's own database image (the twenty migrations, RLS on, sessions as app_user with the JWT sub and the scope GUC set as the edge's rest-handler sets them). The ledger 020–024 is idempotent script by script: every statement is DROP IF EXISTS, CREATE OR REPLACE or ON CONFLICT, so a script applied again from the top converges on both ledgers, which is the property a refused or half-applied publish needs and no comment yet states. The feed's reader-relative policy was measured at two hundred thousand rows, the one-string application the edge gives a script was reproduced on Postgres, and the feed's source key was probed with a chosen id. What the next sprint should take first is cheap: the feed's key, a check that freezes published scripts, and three sentences that say what the tree does not.

        1. medium — decision-news names two shapes for the feed at scale, "a fan-out inbox or an index by actor and time", and the second does not work. At 200,157 feed rows a reader with no friends walks the whole time index under the policy (57 ms, 200k buffers, every row removed by the filter), a reader with one quiet friend the same (72 ms for five rows a year old), a founder with five active friends 0.17 ms; with (actor_id, at DESC, id DESC) added and the read written as a join on the friend list, the planner still walks idx_feed_at for a top-twenty across friends (65 ms). Only a per-reader inbox bounds the sparse read: one row per friend per doing, written by the same triggers over the actor's friendship rows, policy reader_id = auth_uid(), index (reader_id, at DESC, id DESC), the unfriend trigger deleting the pair's rows and feed_forget deleting by source across readers; its cost is friends × doings on write. And the sparse reader is the common one on a demo site: every fresh guest has no friends, so each início costs a full walk, linear in the table (about 30 ms at 10⁵ rows, 300 at 10⁶). Strike the index from the decision, name the inbox with its write cost, and keep the threshold. Disposition: fixed in the words, recorded in the work — decision-news and the brief name the fan-out inbox as the feed's next shape, for the edge's visibility and for the sparse reader alike; the index stays until the inbox replaces the table, since it costs nothing the inbox does not remove.
        2. medium — the feed's one-row-per-source key is uq_feed_source (source_id) over three tables whose ids the client chooses: 011 grants id on scrap, membership and testimonial_draft, and 015 carries the draft's id into testimonial. Reproduced: Letícia drafts a testimonial for her friend Patrícia with the id of a public scrap; 021's guard passes it (it checks testimonial alone); Patrícia's approval then fails inside 015's definer with duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_feed_source" — a testimonial its subject can never approve, handed to them by its writer, and the screen's refusal blames the approval. A join whose chosen id is a scrap's fails the same way, self-inflicted. The key is (kind, source_id), with feed_forget deleting by TG_TABLE_NAME's kind as well as source; a NOT EXISTS over the two other public tables in 021 is the other fix and the worse one. Disposition: fixed — the feed's unique is (kind, source_id) in the program, the forget triggers delete by kind (TG_ARGV), the backfill conflicts on the pair; a draft minted with a scrap's id approves.
        3. medium — the ledger discipline. Sprint 5 edited two published scripts in place, 005 through the picture rule and 020 for the pictures and the fifteenth person, and paid with --reset, which drops every guest, scrap and rating the live site held; the turn-18 disposition says "future picture changes are forward migrations" and nothing holds it. Decision 27 says "sprint 5 decides it" and the brief carries it undecided into the next; and the shape both name, a refresh on the ticker once a day, does not close what the sprint 4 finding named. The stepping channel survives any cadence: a rater steps their own level 0 to 3 across four days and reads the others' sum from four means (with three raters, the sum of two friends' levels); the unfriend's drop in the count survives too, dated to a day instead of a second. A daily refresh closes only the second-resolution dating of a friend's vote. The honest decision is one of: accept the residual as what a public mean of few raters is and say so without promising a closing shape; or raise the floor to five and add hysteresis (the public row moves only when the mean crosses a whole level, one more column the refresh keeps), which narrows the channel and dulls the live mean; noise is out, by the no-randomness rule.         Verdict: approve with findings. The decision's central argument holds, and not by luck: it was forced on a throwaway database built from the app's own image (PostgreSQL 18.0, the twenty migrations, RLS on, two sessions as app_user with a JWT sub and the scope GUC), with pg_sleep pinning each interleaving. Reply first and uncommitted: the delete blocked two seconds on the reply's KEY SHARE, then the 022 guard refused it with "a topic with replies stays"; topic and reply both stand. Delete first and uncommitted: the reply's foreign-key check blocked on the exclusive tuple lock, then failed with 23503 once the delete committed; topic gone, no orphan. Delete first then rolled back: the reply waited and landed. The window inside the guard, a sleep planted after its EXISTS saw no reply: the reply arriving in the window still blocked on the row and failed on commit, because GetTupleForTrigger takes the exclusive tuple lock before a BEFORE ROW trigger fires, and the guard, VOLATILE, takes its snapshot after that lock, so READ COMMITTED gives it the committed reply. And the shape 022's comment rejects, the guard as a DELETE policy NOT EXISTS: the policy read under the statement's snapshot before the lock, the lock then returned TM_Ok with nothing to re-evaluate, and the cascade erased a committed reply — the exact violation, reproduced. No advisory lock is needed; the FK's lock is the serialization. The driver's twenty rounds against the launched stack passed here too (2 replies landed, 18 deletes won), and the seven screen and catalogue tests pass. The three-rater refresh is safe: three raters committing together under 023's advisory lock serialized (2.0, 3.0, 5.0 s) and the row read raters=3; the same three with the lock line removed left three karma rows and no smiley row, so the lock is load-bearing, and its cost is that raters of one person serialize their whole transactions, milliseconds under PostgREST. A build check in the integrate closure is the right tier for these clauses: they are about PostgREST, auth and RLS together, which no loop test has, and a replay battery is recorded requests, which can neither mint guests nor race two sessions; the guests are right because the integrate stack is disposable and the demo seed stays untouched.

        1. medium — the race block of tests/ledger.ts (lines 106–122) is a smoke, not a proof: twenty HTTP rounds cannot force an interleaving, nothing asserts that both outcomes occurred, and a run where every round resolved the same way would pass identically. The proof is the lock-order argument, which only a two-session SQL script with a planted sleep can exercise; the five interleavings above took five seconds on the database image alone. Either state in decision-driver that the rounds are a smoke over an argument proven at the SQL tier, or carry that script as a check against the closure's database (two connections, pg_sleep), where it is deterministic. Disposition: fixed — the decision says so now: the rounds are a smoke and the proof is the lock order forced at the SQL tier; ten of the twenty rounds give one side a head start and assert that order's outcome, so both paths are exercised on every run.
        2. low — 022's comment is right that the guard must stay a trigger, but the argument rests on a property it does not name: topic_delete_guard is VOLATILE by default and must stay so. Marked STABLE, its EXISTS would reuse the statement's snapshot, taken before the tuple lock, and miss the reply that committed while the delete waited. One clause in the comment pins it. Disposition: fixed — 022's comment pins VOLATILE and says why, with the DELETE-policy shape it rejects.
        3. low — a reply to a topic whose delete has committed is refused by 017's member guard with "only members post in a community's forum" (its topic join is empty), 400; one arriving while the delete is uncommitted is refused by the foreign key, 409. Two codes and a misleading sentence for one situation. Correct either way, and the ledger accepts any non-201, but the screen's refusal would blame membership for a vanished topic. Disposition: fixed — the race asserts the losing reply answers 400 (017, the topic gone) or 409 (the key, the delete open), and says which is which.
        4. low — the filtered / refused split matches the SQL: every filtered case is a USING arm (011 scrap and testimonial deletes, community and app_user updates; 022's topic delete; 006's testimonial_pending update; 023's karma update) and every refused case a RAISE or CHECK (017, 021, 022, 023, 005's CHECKs, the fan pair's unique index). But refused treats 400, 403 and 409 as one class and inspects only one message, so a CHECK that fell away with a unique index catching the case instead, or a WITH CHECK 403 standing in for a guard's 400, passes unseen. Give the helper the expected code: 400 for a raise or CHECK, 409 for a unique pair. Disposition: fixed — refused takes the exact status and a word of the refusing rule's message; the self-rating turned out to be 023's friend rule, not the CHECK, which the driver now says.
        5. low — the driver is one deno run script of sequential asserts, so the first failure hides every clause after it, and the ids it decides are only in comments. As Deno.test blocks named by their acceptance ids, each clause reports on its own and the integrate log reads as the ledger does. Disposition: fixed — the driver is one Deno.test with a step per clause, named by its acceptance ids; the integrate log reads as the ledger does.

        Verdict: approve with findings, two majors reproduced on the running database in rolled-back transactions. Shape scoping is sound: each table's scope column is generated from the writer, the subject or the public scope, every shape filters on it, and no UPDATE can re-point a key, so a mirrored copy lands in the subject's scope by construction; the public table holds approved rows alone, demo included; approve is the request accept's shape and its trigger chain terminates.

        1. major — the guard ran as a definer before RLS and author_id was grantable, so a stranger's hand-made insert naming another writer got "one testimonial per person" where a private draft existed and a permission error otherwise: a privacy oracle, and the request guard in 015 had the same one through from_id. Disposition: fixed — the guard runs as the caller, its reads being public tables and the caller's own drafts; 011 grants neither author_id nor from_id, which default to the token and which no form sends.
        2. major — two concurrent drafts for one pair both passed the guard's read. Disposition: fixed — unique pairs on the draft and on the public table; publish moves the pair in one transaction, so they never collide.
